title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-10)
text: To form a C2 the previous candle's low must be taken and the gap must hold: close, open, reversal, continuation; not much deeper than that area. "So it'd be price closes there, opens up, reversal, continuation. That's if we're forming a C2."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-10)
text: Late in the candle there are only three acceptable scenarios: immediate expansion over (continuation), sweep the low then go, or sweep with a larger wick and wait for the next candle. "There's now three options. One, it immediately expands over, forms a continuation. Two, sweeps out the low, then goes. Three, sweeps out the low with a larger wick. Waits for the next candle to go."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-10)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-10)
text: After a CISD, 50% of the CISD candle bodies should be respected for a clean trend in that candle. "Well, if we have a change in the state of delivery, we want to see 50% of the bodies be respected."

Pre-open he ranks relative strength YM strongest, ES middle, NQ weakest (NQ's 4H candle below its open on the 15m-4H TTFM layout), favours YM for longs into its previous month's high, says gold is 'tapped out' after a run of continuations (do not fade it), dollar bearish and its targets hit (EURUSD/GBPUSD bullish), and oil expanding into previous-day lows. At the 9:30 open the 15m, 30m and 4H candles all supported higher; ES and then YM took his marked highs (~7,694 ES; YM blue line ~53,150-53,200, which he later calls its previous month's high), and he teaches the time-based exit: 9:45 first target (15m expansion candle close), 10:00 second target (30m and 4H close), which he writes on the chart. After 9:45 indices consolidated, so nothing more to do; a 1m-15m gold continuation-long idea failed (the 15m candle made too large a wick and disrespected the EQ), and he uses it to show why continuations keep you out of losses and, after 10:00, how a failed valid model becomes an invalidation trade lower into previous lows (~4,038 line). No trades were taken; most of the second half is Q&A (risk per trade from drawdown not account size, position size versus stop width, one trade a day, why the model ignores candle 5 after a C2-C3-C4 expansion, how his indicator works). Day type: Wednesday, day after the US midterm elections (Nov 3, 2026); huge-range expansion day on indices and gold (he says ADRs already hit before the open); NY open expanded 9:30-10:00 then consolidated; gold consolidated then failed lower after 10:00 Higher-timeframe read: YM1! 4H bullish - Relative strength: YM strongest, ES middle, NQ weakest. YM's 4H candle is well above its open. 'Obviously not a normal daily range, but it's holding up in the range, hasn't its targets, so reaching for its previous month's high.' Preferred asset for longs. DOL: previous month's high (YM blue line ~53,150-53,200 read from the 15m axis; YM took it ~09:44 per 'YM hit that high'); ES1! 4H bullish - Middle asset; 4H candle above its open. 'Can also look for that high on ES. You can go mark those out.' DOL: marked high, blue line ~7,694 (read from 15m axis); taken at ~09:35-09:38, then 9:30 15m candle closed near ~7,730; NQ1! 4H neutral - Weakest index: 'Just look at the 4-hour candle, right? What is it doing? It's down here below its open.' He would not use NQ as a long target; only a short target if bearish. Strength later rotated (NQ catching up at 09:31).; GC1! 4H bullish - Yesterday's idea: move into a gap as retracement or reversal, then reversal, continuation, continuation, continuation, expansion. Failure swings hit, 'gold is pretty much tapped out for me'. 4H still aligned bullish: 'There's nothing bearish here. Not in, at least not until 10 a.m.' He does not fade the daily range but expects consolidation, retracement or a new phase of price. DOL: already took the previous day's high; equal highs above (1H blue lines ~4,082 and ~4,097 read from axis); CL1! 1H bearish - Expansion, consolidation, run out the high of the consolidation, expansion, retracement, new expansion into previous day lows. 'So we can get a new phase of price or continue to trend depending on if we form a retracement here.' DOL: previous day lows (already reached); DXY 1D bearish - Bearish on the dollar since yesterday's stream; it has hit its targets ('another run of the low'), which is bullish for foreign currencies. Prefers GBPUSD/EURUSD (strong against the dollar) over yen crosses; not a fan of the yen. DOL: targets already hit; 6E1! 1D bullish - Dollar bearish makes euro bullish; 'So I took out the low there. Probably just going to consolidate it like that.' GBPUSD/EURUSD: 'we get that expansion into those highs, ideally over into this range high.' DOL: range high (no level stated); BTC 1D neutral - Idea was a low forming at one of two places; it looks like it is forming. 'If we get a closure through here, that would be a potential continuation higher.' Key levels: ES1! marked high ~7,694 (blue line, read from 15m axis) - the high he expects ES to reach into at the open; taken ~09:35-09:38; YM1! previous month's high, blue line ~53,150-53,200 (approximate axis read) - YM target; he hand-draws a red projected path up through it; YM hit it ~09:44; ES1! 9:30 15m expansion candle, high ~7,732, closed near its high - time-based target: hold to 9:45 close, partial off there; GC1! 1H blue lines ~4,097, ~4,082 (equal-highs area above) and ~4,038 (lower line; at 10:21 he says it is 'just this previous high') - upside liquidity while bullish; ~4,038 becomes the downside reach for the invalidation trade; GC1! 1m: session high ~4,062 (blue line), indicator EQ zone ~4,046-4,049 (yellow box), 9:30-area low ~4,043 - 1m-15m continuation long idea needed price to hold the EQ zone and run back through ~4,062; losing it led to the run of the lows; RTY1! previous month's high, blue line ~2,887 on the daily - already hit, so Russell is 'the weakest asset on a bullish day' SMT: NQ1!/ES1!/YM1! Relative strength pre-open: YM strongest, ES middle, NQ weakest (NQ 4H candle below its open). After ES hit its target the strength switched: NQ, which had been catching up, became the weakest again, letting YM trend to its target.; NQ1!/ES1!/YM1! Equal highs on the indices with only one asset taking them out: 'one asset took it out, but I don't really trust it'.; GC1!/XAUEUR/XAUGBP Gold SMT on the high at ~09:53 (indicator SMT(Auto) compares XAUEUR, XAUGBP): 'There is one thing is there is an SMT on this high. I just don't really like it.' Earlier: even with an SMT for a short, the CISD took too long and the low was swept, so it became a consolidation, not a reversal.; RTY1!/YM1!/ES1! At 10:24: 'RTY leading the way, so that's usually meaning YM is going to start falling.' YM took a month high and small caps react; if they lead the downside ES falls, which is confusing because ES is currently the strongest. Context: Day after the US midterm elections; he attributes the large index move to who gets elected, their policies and control of House and Senate. Not a normal daily range: ADRs already hit before the open. Session timing: 9:30 open; 15m expansion candle to 9:45, 30m and 4H candles to 10:00 (4H bullish 'until 10 a.m.'); after 10:00 new 4H candle and ideas re-evaluated. Prep order: Cross-asset sweep before the open: indices relative strength (4H candle vs its open on NQ/ES/YM 15m-4H layout), then gold, silver, oil, dollar, FX (EURUSD/GBPUSD vs yen), Bitcoin > Identify the strongest asset for longs (weakest for shorts) and mark its higher-timeframe target (previous month's high on YM/ES) > At 9:30 check whether the new 15m, 30m and hourly candles support expansion (small wick) > Set time-based targets from the higher-timeframe candle closes (9:45, 10:00) when there is no clean liquidity target > After the expansion, judge the next candle's wick/EQ respect; if it does not support continuation, wait for the next HTF candle (10:00) > After 10:00, if the valid model failed, look at the invalidation direction Scenarios: If the 9:30 15m candle is an expansion candle (small wick, closes into its high) then hold longs until 9:45; if the 30m/4H are also expansion candles hold to 10:00; If BTC closes through the marked level then potential continuation higher; If the gold 1m/15m candle stays small-wicked and holds around the indicator EQ zone then continuation long back through the ~4,062 high; if it forms too big a wick, targets are back toward the 15m open, so wait for the next candle or a candle-4 continuation; If gold trades lower than the marked low at ~09:53 then 'it's just going to probably fail to the lows of the range'; If indices after 10:00 open and invalidate the EQ, form a higher low then continuation higher still possible; otherwise 'this is just bearish to me now' and he will not trade it; If a valid model fails to work (gold long after 10:00) then invalidation trade: price goes the other way, into previous lows; If RTY leads lower and small caps reject the previous month's high then YM and ES likely give back some of the morning move, maybe back to the 9:30 price; watch the daily close

text: Q: What makes it an expansion candle? Price forms the high or low early into the candle, using very little time or range, leaving enough time for expansion."

text: Q: Is risking 1% of the drawdown per trade in prop accounts a good idea? Never size from the account size (25k, 1M are arbitrary); you only have the drawdown amount. "How many trades do you want to be able to lose in a row before the account gone?"

text: Q: For an entry in candle 3, do we need a swing formation or can we enter directly on an FVG or OB? title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Q: Can you explain how your indicator works on the chart? A: It marks his model: a swing point (candle 2 or candle 3 closure), then the CISD (find the series of candles that made the low and check for a close over it), plus PSP/SMT, then a T-spot box showing where he wants the wick to form, and protected swings (went into a POI and closed over, so expected to hold). A failed bullish idea usually means an invalidation trade the other way. "Which is find a low, find a series of candles that made it, did it close over? So what my indicator does is it does that for me, plus it looks for PSP, SMT, those type of things."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Q: Let the wick form? A: If the wick forms near the opening price of the higher-timeframe candle it is low risk and high probability to expand; he just wants it to form inside the higher-timeframe box. "If the wick forms near the opening price of the higher timeframe candle, it would be a low risk and high probability to expand."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Q: Why are we bearish on gold here? A: The bullish idea failed; with no bullish idea left it is a bearish idea, reaching into previous lows and the blue line (previous high). This is how invalidation trades work: valid model, it does not work, price goes the other way. "You have have valid model. Valid model doesn't work. If valid model doesn't work, price goes other way. That's literally it, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: An expansion candle (small wick, large body, high/low formed early) closes into its extreme, so the higher-timeframe candle close is a valid target: 9:30 15m candle to 9:45, 30m and 4H to 10:00. "Why would you target 9.45? This is an expansion candle. Expansion candles close into their highs. So right here, you can just hold it till 9.45."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Expansion candle definition: small wick, large body, closes near its high or low, and forms its high or low early in the candle using very little time or range. "An expansion candle has a small wick, a large body. Look, it closes near its high or closes near its low, right? Price forms the high or low early into the candle, using very little time or range, leaving enough time for expansion."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: With no clear liquidity target (e.g. price already beyond the daily range), use time-based exits at higher-timeframe candle closes/opens; it works on every timeframe (monthly expansion trade exits at month end). "If you don't know, if you don't have a target for expansion, you use higher timeframe, candles, flows in time, and basically opens."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: After the expansion candle closes, partial or exit at its close; you do not know whether it continues, retraces, reverses or consolidates. "You don't know now, is this going to continue to expand? That would align with the higher timeframes, but this could also retrace or reverse or consolidate."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: A candle that disrespects the EQ with a weak close can still be tolerated as a small wick, but once the wick grows too large the targets revert toward the HTF candle's open; wait for the next candle (or a candle-4 continuation) instead of entering. "We're already kind of disrespecting the EQ because we have a weaker closure here, and we didn't close into the highs. So I'm allowing it to trade a little bit lower and still considering that a small wick."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: If the current candle does not support expansion in your direction, do not trade it; wait for the next higher-timeframe candle. "But you see how this candle doesn't support expansion higher, so there's no reason to try to trade it, right? You're better off waiting for the next candle"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Trade continuations because they require the market to confirm; when the idea is wrong no continuation forms, so you are wrong without taking a loss. "But there's no entry whatsoever because when you wait for a continuation to form, you're waiting for the market to tell you that it's doing something. When it doesn't do something, that's fine. You just are wrong and you didn't take a loss, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Do not fade a strong expansion / daily range; if the 4H is still aligned, nothing is bearish until that 4H candle closes (10:00). "Because, like I said, don't try to fade. Just don't trade this. Like, if you already miss this move, either sit out or you're, this is still aligned bullish, right? The 4-hour? There's nothing bearish here. Not in, at least not until 10 a.m."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: An SMT reversal idea whose CISD takes too long to form, and that sweeps the low instead, is a consolidation that trades to the other side of the range, not a reversal. "Even if you're looking to trade this lower with the SMT, look how long we take to form the CISD. We don't, and we sweep out the low. So now this is a consolidation to trade to the other side of the range."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Invalidation trade: if a valid model fails to work, price goes the other way. "We have a valid model. Does it work? Nope. Does it work? Nope. Okay, cool. If this valid model doesn't work, price goes the other way. That's it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: The model trades candle 3 and 4 (sometimes candle 2); after three candles of expansion expect a new phase of price and do not look for a candle-5 continuation. "So that's why we look to trade candle 3 and 4 or sometimes candle 2. But after we get three candles or expansion or three candles of movement, we can get a new phase of price."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Do not enter late after a huge range has already been made (entering after ~2,800 points of range and C2-C3-C4 expansion is entering candle 5). "I personally wouldn't have been really looking long at 10AM for myself, just because we've already expanded, we've had a massive range"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: The wick should form inside the higher-timeframe box (T-spot), ideally near the HTF candle's open, which gives low risk and high probability of expansion. "If the wick forms near the opening price of the higher timeframe candle, it would be a low risk and high probability to expand."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Size risk per trade from the drawdown and the number of consecutive losses you want to survive (7-10), never from the nominal account size. "Account size does not matter at all. It's arbitrary. Use the drawdown on it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: A wider stop is handled by reducing position size, not by taking more risk. "You should be adjusting your position size to account for the movement in"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Normally one trade a day maximum. "In terms of risk management, I just take one trade a day normally max."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: If continuation trades keep stopping you out before reaching target, move the entry up one timeframe (e.g. 5m to 15m), because the stop is likely inside a higher-timeframe FVG. "So if you're on the five-minute, you're always getting stopped out, then it goes to your entry. Most likely there's like a 15-minute fair value gap you always get stopped at in. So just go to the 15-minute chart and enter on that."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: With several markets, get the idea from the hourly or 4H first and only then drop to lower timeframes. "So stop trying to go down to the 5-minute on all your assets you watch instead of waiting for an hourly or 4-hour to give you an idea, then going lower."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Direction comes from the daily chart. "Go to the daily chart. Everything should be based off the daily chart."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: For candle-3 entries he prefers an intra-candle CISD; positional entries on an FVG/OB are an acceptable alternative. "I personally prefer intra-candle change in the state of delivery, but you can also take positional entries, that type of stuff."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: In the scalping model a 5-minute CISD confirming the 1-hour is ideal but not required. "You don't need it, but it is ideal."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: CISD = find the low, find the series of candles that made it, and check for a close over it; a protected swing is one that went into a POI and closed over, so it is expected to hold if price continues. "Then we check for the change in the state delivery, right? Which is find a low, find a series of candles that made it, did it close over?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Swing trading uses the daily-hourly pairing; his intraday layout pairs 15m-4H (also 1m-15m on gold, 3m-30m alerts). "When I'm looking to swing trade, I'm usually using the daily and hourly model."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: After a deep retracement that invalidates the EQ, the continuation idea no longer meets the model; it only revives if price invalidates the EQ, forms a higher low and then a continuation. "There's either that idea or we invalidate the EQ, form of the higher low, and the continuation. We'll probably just hop off of it because there's really not much to do when it gets that deep of a retracement."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: When two paths are alive (reversal vs retracement-then-continuation), do nothing and wait for price to show its phase. "Like, do we form a reversal, right? Or do we kind of retrace to then set up for the continuation that way, you know? I don't really know what's going on, so we just wait."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: A sequence of continuations ending in an expansion with its failure swings hit means the move is 'tapped out': expect consolidation, retracement or a new phase of price rather than fading it. "So gold is pretty much Tapped out for me. If you notice all these failure swings right here, it gets hit."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Equal highs taken by only one correlated asset are not trusted. "And one asset took it out, but I don't really trust it. We have equal highs right here, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: He prefers trend-aligned trades; counter-trend trades and trading the invalidation of bias are not his preference. "I don't prefer to take counter trend trades, so up to you."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Use futures, not CFDs, so candle closes are identical across platforms. "Like these are going to close the same on everything because it's futures."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: Once indices have expanded 9:30-10:00 and started consolidating, there is nothing left to do unless already in a position and trailing. "Can it continue higher? Sure. Hopefully it does, but I mean, there's not much to do anymore on it unless you're in a position and you're trailing it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-11-04)
text: An asset that has already hit all its targets is the weakest on a bullish day; skip it. "Russell looks weak. The weakest asset on a bullish day. Because it hit all its targets."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-28)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-28)

All the information is available for free. "Mainly, indicator, access to me, the course is the course, you don't get the course on my website."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Q: I studied all your videos and want to learn more (SMT, correlation...). A: If you don't understand the basics of the model, adding SMT, PSP and other tools won't help and keeps you from learning. They aren't bad, but build the foundation first. "If you don't understand the basics of my model, adding SMT, adding PSP, adding all these things to it is not going to help you."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Q: I was right on gold being bullish. A: There's a big difference between calling a direction and acting on it before the breakout with an entry. "there's a big difference between saying, hey, guys, gold's bearish right here or bullish right there and then doing it before it breaks out"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Identify the strongest and weakest of the correlated assets every day; the previous closure tells you, and 9:30 makes it obvious. "Relative strength, which was strongest, which was weakest. If you can answer that question most days, you're going to keep yourself from a lot of headache, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: You can read relative strength from the first one-minute closure after 9:30 (9:31). "You could literally wait for 9.31 and get the relative strength by just looking at that one-minute closure."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: For longs, trade the strongest asset; never long the weakest asset (and short the weakest when bearish). "If you were going to long, right, you want to trade the strongest asset. You'd be trading this on YM. Don't try to trade the weakest asset."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Being right on direction isn't enough: shorting the strong asset or longing the weak one can still get you killed. "YM here, you're getting absolutely killed, right? If you long NQ here, you're getting killed."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Unless the market is consolidating, correlated assets trend together; the asset falling behind may be 'lying' and catch up. "Unless you're going to completely consolidate, correlated assets trend together."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: If the strongest asset is going to continue, you want the weakest asset to sweep a low and reverse first, because that creates SMT. "if YN is going to get a continuation higher, I like to see the weakest asset, spoken about this before, reverse, because what does that do? That then makes SMT."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: SMT is not required to take a trade. "No, you don't need SMT for a trade."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: ES generally doesn't lead; NQ or YM leads. "Generally, ES never leads. One of the others will lead, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Once one asset has printed several expansion candles, it consolidates or retraces while the others catch up; you can trade the laggard's continuation then. "So now YM's has its multiple expansion candles. This is now where the other can catch up while it consolidates."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: A 9:30 expansion usually lasts two candles: to 9:45 if the 15m is an expansion candle, to 10:00 if the 30m stays one; then the new 4H candle brings new ideas. "Generally, when you get a 9.30 expansion, it goes until two times, 9.45 or 10. Because this 15-minute candle is an expansion candle, so it should continue until 9.45."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Align with the daily candle; don't fade the opposing higher-timeframe candle. "So like on this, I'm bearish. Why? Because I want to align with the daily candle."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: After an expansion, expect a new phase of price (retracement, reversal or consolidation) before a new continuation; Monday after last week's expansion was that new phase. "Yesterday is what I would say a new phase of price, because I'm not expecting us to just continue to trend the whole time. Need some sort of retracement, reversal, retracement, so we can get a new continuation."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: If the profile shows no intraday reversal against your bias, keep the bias. "There is absolutely nothing here telling me it is bullish. So then I just remain bearish. That's it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Don't trade from the middle of a move: wait for a new swing to form so there is something to trade away from and a sensible stop. "So you'd have to wait for the open for something to form to actually look to trade away from."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: If you trust the low (or high) of the day, you can trade away from it. "As long as you trust a low of the day, you can trade away, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Entry sequence: every entry needs a swing point and then a closure through it, which forms the protected swing; the ideal is both happening at once (a C2/C3 closure), but that isn't required. "To form a protected swing, you have to have a swing point and then a closure through."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: A return from a CISD level also creates a protected swing if it happens in a point of interest. "If it's in a point of interest, yeah."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Prefer CISD over IFVG as the entry. "CISD is correct."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Continuations are far easier than reversals; wait for a continuation instead of trying to long the low of the day. "You don't need to trade the reversal. Reversals are hard to trade, guys. Like, continuations are far easier."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: In a bearish idea, no lower high means no trade; it just means the trend continues against you. "If we can't form a lower high, there's no trade, right? Because then this is just saying it's a continuation of that trend."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Wait for the higher-timeframe candle closure first, then a continuation or lower high; that saves you from losses when the idea is wrong. "We save ourself a potential loss so far. By waiting for what? The higher time from candle closure first, but also a continuation or a lower high."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Trends happen early in an expansion candle; once a candle has used too much time and range, stop trading it and reevaluate at the next candle's open and close. "if we're going to trend, when is it going to do it? In an expansion candle. Early into the candle forms, it's how it goes. So I'm better off waiting for 10-15"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: When a setup needs to work, look for a very aggressive candle back into the range or away from the high; without it the idea will likely chop out. "you want to see like a very aggressive candle back into the range. Otherwise, The whole idea just may just chop out."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: After sweeping a low, the next move should expand away from it: price forms a gap and a new move comes out of that gap, not a reversal. "normally what you want to see is this form a gap, and then you have a new move out of that, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: On a reversal day with a large wick, targets are the daily open, then intraday liquidity, then the previous-day low or high; don't expect an expansion. "So whenever you have a reversal day with a large wick, your targets are always daily open and then intraday liquidity, right? And then you can look towards previous day low or previous day high if you need to go further."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Once a reversal trade hits its targets, the move is over for you, whatever price does next. "This move would be over for me, right? This move can do whatever it wants. Because if you're trading this reversal, like we said, those are your targets."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: A short after price hits a higher-timeframe target is valid as an intraday reversal, with adjusted (smaller) targets. "You're adjusting your targets for sure. I mean, it is valid in terms of a short after you hit a higher time from target."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: In a consolidation, a range trade needs a sweep of one side while the opposite extreme holds, then a 15m/30m swing, targeting the other side of the range. "So you'd want to see a sweep of this side of the range, right? And you want to see this high remain."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: He trades expansions only; a separate consolidation strategy fades breaks outside a range back into it. "I prefer to just focus on the expansions personally, but that's how you would do it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Avoid trading away from failure swings on both sides of a range. "I don't like to trade away from all these failure swings on each side."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Continuations that form while sweeping a higher-timeframe key level tend to fail. "When you have the continuation that forms as it's like sweeping out a higher timeframe key level, that's my in your why your continuations fail video."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Scalping model: trade the continuation only when the hourly and the 15m are both continuing in the same direction. "You want to trade the continuation on the hourly? And on the 15, right, all of that all aligned together, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Earlier in the day the intraday-reversal timeframes are 4H/1H; in New York you can adjust them slightly. "Earlier in the day, it's 4-hour, 1-hour. As you get into New York, you can adjust things slightly different."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Once you're further into a continuation (e.g. candle 4), separation from the prior reversal level matters less, because price has already shown it can reverse there. "if we're in candle 4, Christ already showed me it can reverse there. It doesn't really matter as much anymore once you're further in the continuation."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: If Asia and London already expanded and price is consolidating, lower your expectations for the NY move. "if Asia and London expands, I mean, you gotta realize it's pretty, price is consolidating a little. Like, you can't have the largest expectations right away."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Missing the first entry is not the end; later continuation entries are available, and waiting for them also tells you when you're wrong. "Because a lot of you guys think that if you miss that very first entry, it's over for you. It's not."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: If things are confusing, don't force a trade; some days and weeks are unclear, and that's normal. "If stuff's confusing, you don't have to force a trade onto it, right? You can be patient."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Learn the model's foundation before adding tools like SMT, PSP or correlation. "It's just stop trying to add things when you don't actually understand the foundation."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: A bias you can't position for intraday isn't a trade; catching a move like GU would need a higher-timeframe position with a wider stop. "The bias is there, but unless I'm positioning on a higher timeframe, putting my stop lower, I'm not catching that intraday, personally."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: He watches several assets on synced side-by-side charts (NQ/ES/YM panes) to compare relative strength intraday. "We'll take a watch on all these assets at once, kind of intraday like that. Helps you see relative strength, relative weakness, all of that, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Mistake: Blindly longing the weakest asset at its low because a correlated asset is rallying. Fix: Wait for the weak asset to actually reverse (sweep + CISD / intraday reversal), or long the strongest asset's continuation instead.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Mistake: Trying to long the low of the day (reversal trading). Fix: Wait for 9:30 and a continuation to form, then trade the continuation.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Mistake: Shorting in the middle of the range with no structure, which forces a stop far away. Fix: Wait for the open and a new swing to form so there is something to trade away from.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Mistake: Calling gold 'bullish as hell' off one 15m candle and fading the daily candle. Fix: Align with the daily candle; one candle doesn't change the read; watch the phases of price.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Mistake: Expecting a large NY move when Asia and London already expanded and price is consolidating. Fix: Lower expectations and targets on consolidation days.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Mistake: New traders stacking every confluence (OB, FVG, breaker, MSS) or adding SMT/PSP before understanding the base model. Fix: Learn the foundation (free course, his model only) first, then add tools that actually help.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Mistake: Believing that missing the first entry means the trade is over. Fix: Later continuation entries form; waiting for them also shows when the idea is wrong.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Mistake: Expecting to understand what the market is doing every single day. Fix: Accept unclear days and weeks as normal; don't force trades.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Mistake: Claiming you were 'right' on a direction call without having entered before the breakout. Fix: What counts is executing an entry before the move, not naming the direction.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-20)
text: Mistake: Fixating on one index ('YM always moves further and faster'). Fix: The leader changes; trade whichever asset is stronger or weaker that day.

text: Q: Why bullish on YM and bearish on NQ? A: The other way round: bearish on YM off the open (into its low) and bullish on NQ off the open (into its high). "So the reason I say 4-hour and 15 a lot of times is because it can help people not get chopped up."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-06)
text: Q: Why do we use the EQ? A: EQ mechanically decides whether a wick is small enough for expansion. If the wick stays within the EQ, price can still expand in the bias direction. If price retraces past it ('all the way down here'), it can still be bullish but will not expand; it will likely just return to the daily open or the intraday highs. "The EQ is what we use to mechanically determine what is a small enough wick for expansion."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-10-06)
text: Q: What are candle 1, candle 2 and candle 3? A: Just a numbering. Candle 2 is always the swing high or low; candle 1 is arbitrary, the one before it; candle 3 follows candle 2; candle 4 follows candle 3. Every candle 2 is a swing point, but he only cares about a candle 2 or candle 3 closure at a point of interest. Example: a C2 that sweeps a high in a gap and closes back below qualifies; a plain swing high without that closure does not. "A swing point I'm interested in has to be a candle 2 closure or a candle 3 closure at a point of interest."

This is not a continuation I would personally enter because of the location. You're below these lows, you're below previous day low. It's fine to trail stop there. I don't like to enter breakouts like that."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-23)
text: Location in the dealing range matters: a short entered low in the dealing range is not ideal (poor R:R, failure swings before the first target). "Not super ideal because you're quite low in the range, right, in the dealing range."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-23)
text: He doesn't like breakouts that have no swings below them; a breakout before the range high is taken is acceptable. "I don't mind trading a breakout before the range high is taken. Not a huge fan of breakouts without any swings below."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-23)
text: When price takes a range low, the read is binary: manipulation (sweep the low and go higher) or failure to manipulate (break down lower). "Do we manipulate this low to go higher? Or do we fail to manipulate the low to break down lower? It is really just two things."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-23)
text: If a C2 high remains, price must invalidate that wick before a short; if it sweeps the high, wait for a new C2. "So then the whole idea is if this high is going to remain, right, it may or may not, then it would have to invalidate this kind of wick here. If it goes and sweeps out the new high, then you kind of have to just wait for a new C2."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-23)
text: On an expansion day you can generally hold to the close; otherwise take profit at the correlated draw (e.g. pound/euro shorts held until DXY reaches its daily gap). "If you're short into Pound or Euro, I prefer Pound, then you can hold until the dollar hits that level. A good profit-taking target or towards the end of the day, then an expansion day, so you can generally hold till the close."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: Waiting for a continuation protects you from bad reversal ideas: if price retraces into an FVG but never closes through it, there is no continuation and no trade. "How do you save yourself from These ideas. You just wait for continuations."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: Always know what the daily candle is doing, even when executing on the 1m. "Even if I'm trading a one-minute time frame, I'm still understanding what the daily candle's doing."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: Previous day high/low is liquidity because yesterday's traders put their stops there. "Where are you going to put your stop loss? Probably on a previous day high or a swing high. So that then becomes the area where liquidity is, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: A New York reversal profile (previous day high taken, failure swings) has limited targets when price opened in the middle of the range; don't expect it to go far. "on a normal New York reversal, you don't, like, you're not trying to target this, the weird middle ground. That's why I'm not looking for it to go crazy far."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: No kill zones: if the higher-timeframe wick has formed, an entry at 6:45 is as valid as one at 8:30. "I'm not going to wait for the kill zone if price forms its wick on the higher timeframe and starts to trade lower, right? Then I can get on side with it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: No model wins every time; expect losses. "no model works all the time. You're never going to have a 100% win rate."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: Use CISD instead of BOS/MSS/CHoCH: find the high, find the series of candles that made it, and a close through it is the shift. "I always find the high, I find the series of candles, I made the high, close through it, that's it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: Top-down: daily for directional bias, then 4H/1H for structure (FVG, daily EQ, swing points) to find where price should react once the daily wick has formed, then align a fractal model. "Your goal here is to find an area where you expect price to react after you've already lit the wick form of the daily candle."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: Entry sequence: swing point to trade away from, CISD (he doesn't trade the reversal itself), wait for a continuation, enter, stop on the protected swing, target 2R. "I take an entry, I put my stop loss on the protected swing, my indicator marks it out, and then I can look for 2R."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: Have a bias before you trade; without one you are pattern trading. "Have a bias before you look to trade. Otherwise, you're just simply trying to pattern trade."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: The wick has formed when price, at your area and in your bias direction, expands and closes over (bullish) or sweeps the previous level and closes below (bearish); time matters only because it defines the HTF candles (9:30, 9:45, 10:00). "Right here, price sweeps out the previous, closes below. Do you think the wick has formed? If yes, then you can trade it lower."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: Use YM mainly as a relative-strength gauge to trade NQ/ES. "I use it more as a relative strength indicator to trade the other assets."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: He enters continuations on any timeframe; 15m setups positioned 6-8am before the open, and hourly/daily ones, are among his favourites. "I enter continuations on any time frame. It does not really matter the time frame to me. My favorite trades are honestly the higher time frame ones, like the hourly, daily chart."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: MMXM maps onto the fractal model: smart money reversal = swing point, target = the swing low that made the swing high; equivalently, candle 2 closure + CISD targeting the 4H swing low / previous day low. title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: On a no-bias day with decoupled indices, either path is tradable by reaction (strong asset to its high, weak asset to its low). "Like I said, it's a reaction game. So it's like you could either trade it into the slow or trade it into the high."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: Don't trust a V-shape reversal against your bias; the level it would need to respect if it were genuine decides it, and a closure below that sends price to the actual lows. "You see this nice V-shape reversal? I don't trust it. So what? This is the area you'd have to respect if it was bullish, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: To fade a lower-timeframe bullish CISD, you need an asset to run a high (form a swing point) and then close below or form a lower high; without that lower high there is nothing to do. "But if price never forms a lower high, there's nothing to do."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)
text: Reverse engineer in hindsight rather than bar-replay guessing: for each move ask how you could have got on side, which timeframe shows reversal + continuation, the R:R, whether highs were taken, and the draw on liquidity. title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-16)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-09)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-09)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-09-01)

His tweet example: no management (2R or -1R) would have put a viewer up an extra 6R. Learn management later. "So early on, I normally say, don't worry about managing your position. You have enough to worry about with taking a trade."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Do you trade the lagging asset? A: Never. If NQ is the weakest he will never trade YM short; the middle one is OK. "Can you trade the middle one? Sure. I never trade the very lagging asset."

text: Q: Why didn't the indicator mark anything here? A: Mechanically it is not a setup because it would need to sweep the high; but because of the SMT you can still treat it as a candle 2 / reversal candle. "Well, because mechanically with my model, this isn't a setup, because it would need to sweep this high to be a setup. But because of the SMT, you can still treat this like a candle too, as a reversal candle."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Can you do an update video on your New York Open routine? A: His routine: get to the chart, look for maybe three minutes, that's it (got to charts ~09:25). Journaling is great early on but he no longer needs it. "Get to chart. Look at it for maybe three minutes. That's it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Do you trade London? A: No, he sleeps. "No, I don't take trades in London session, because I sleep."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: What is that range / up-close candle? A: It is just candle 2; it's all fractal: on a daily chart you'd say it should respect the EQ and go lower, same on the 1m. When scalping he sometimes enters on a sweep with a tiny stop. "If you saw this on a daily chart, you'd say, oh, this should respect the EQ and go lower. So that's the same thing on the one-minute chart, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: When would you expect a protected swing to fail and price re-sweep, then continue with the trend? A: When significant liquidity has been taken out: it takes the liquidity, re-sweeps the protected swing, then goes. He is still working out how to explain it mechanically; when it happens he zooms out. "It is when we have taken out some sort of significant liquidity."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Do you use double purge? A: No, he doesn't think like that. "I don't really use it, I don't really think like that, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Price disrespected the EQ; why is it not bullish? A: A closure through the EQ does not switch bias. It can invalidate the bias only when paired with other things including the daily profile. There is no bullish structure and the daily profile is bearish, so it just means a large wick: adjust expectations to the EQ around the open or intraday lows. Also: he picks the consolidation low as target where most people pick the V-shaped low. "A closure through the EQ does not equal switch bias. It can mean the invalidation of the bias when it's paired with other things along with the daily profile."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Why start at the 1-hour, not the daily? A: He started at the daily at the beginning of the stream. "I start at the daily at the beginning of the stream."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: What would you want to see to be bullish? A: Nothing today; only if it ripped back up and closed there, and even then he would not trade it today, he would look for it Monday. "There's nothing that today can do right now to be bullish, unless it was like... Ripped all the way up here and closed there. And at that case, I'm still not going to trade that today. I would look for that on Monday"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Premium/discount? A: He does not use discount and premium like ICT; he uses it the opposite way. See his 'Using EQ for continuations' video. "I don't use discount and premium like ICT teaches it. I use it the opposite way."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Do you trade under or above the open price? A: It depends on the daily profile. "I trade above or below the opening price. It depends on the daily profile."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Can you make more videos about gold for day traders? A: The model is fractal: the same on every asset and every timeframe. Mainly trades indices, also gold, oil, commodities. "My model is fractal. It's the same on every asset. It's the same on any timeframe."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Long on a C2 candle with an IC-CISD formed in London, targeting today's EQ? A: 'Actually fire.' It is a range, so target the EQ or the range. Refine on the 5m or take it on the hourly or 15m: 15m gets the closure through, stop on the protected swing. Demonstrated in replay with a long position tool (stop 35.5 pts, target 116 pts, R:R 3.27). For overnight sessions he uses the 15m because lower timeframes are sloppy. "Here's the thing is you're trying to trade this reversal. Look at what you have. You have a range. That makes sense. And then if you're trying to target this, what do we have? EQ and the range."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Is there a mechanical way to define consolidation? A: You get used to seeing it; it is a high and a low that price stays within for a period of time. "it's a high and a low that price stays within for a period of time."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Stuck after 3 years, what to focus on? (John) A: Be specific: strategy issue, no strategy, tilt/revenge, or not following your process. When John said he can't find one consistent strategy: learn this one model free on the website, follow it, stop learning random stuff and ignore social media. "Go focus on one strategy. You can do this all for free."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: 4 years studying every day makes me realise how inconsistent I am. A: You don't need new information after four years; apply it and stop making avoidable mistakes. Cycle he sees: loss, oversize, tilt, blow account, go learn more ICT instead of fixing sizing. "You need to simply stop doing dumb stuff. It's literally it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Do you backtest with Claude AI? A: No; backtesting is for learning the model and what you want to see (reps). He doesn't backtest anymore. "backtesting is how you learn what you want to see. Get the reps in."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Why not add quarter SMT on the 6-hour? Do strategies decay? A: He doesn't need to add anything. His strategy is based on swing points; the market must put in a swing point to reverse, so it will not decay. "For the market to form a reversal, it has to put in a swing point. That's just simple truth."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: How do I confirm my daily bias (daily profile)? A: Watch his 'intraday reversals' video. "you're going to watch this video called intraday reversals, and that's going to answer your question."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: Do you ever take pre-open trades? A: Only with bias, an aligned daily profile and an invalidation he trusts not to be swept by the 09:30 volatility. For swing trades he just enters at market, sets the stop and goes to bed. "The only way I will do a pre-open trade is if I have bias, daily profile aligns, and then I have an invalidation. I trust to not be swept out by vol at 9.30."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: When is a good time to trade ES instead of NQ/YM? A: When NQ is weakest and already through its low, YM strongest and reversed off a high, and ES is in the middle and has not reached its low yet: trade ES back to that low. Today set up for ES but did not work. "NQ is weakest, YM strongest, ES is in the middle. NQ hits some low here and then gets a continuation through it. ES is not to this low yet, right? And YM just reversed off something up here. So then I would trade ES back to this low"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: I have a strong short bias on S&P/NASDAQ and feel uneasy taking longs. A: If you trade the 3m and hold 30-60 minutes, the monthly view doesn't matter; it matters if you enter on the 4H. Your bias timeframe should match where your intraday timeframe is. "If you're trading the four-hour as an entry, sure, then that starts to matter. It depends where your intraday timeframe is"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: There was an IFVG that got inversed; why didn't that trade work? A: Not his strategy; he doesn't use IFVGs that way. "That's not my strategy. I don't use that."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Q: How do you handle a winning trade that reverses and hits your stop? A: You entered expecting the stop at one spot and the target at the other; if the stop is hit, you were wrong. "If it hits your stop loss, then you were wrong. Not really that crazy."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: A close through the daily EQ is a soft invalidation, not a bias switch: it means the wick is too large to expect expansion, so keep the bias and cut targets to the daily open / liquidity around the open / intraday lows. "A closure through the EQ does not equal switch bias. It can mean the invalidation of the bias when it's paired with other things along with the daily profile."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Bias for the day comes from the daily chart plus the daily profile; an overnight grind up with no trusted low of day is a retracement for a New York reversal, so do not be bullish off it. "But when we just grind up, I'm viewing this as a retracement for New York to reverse."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: On a reversal candle (large wick, small body) expect price to close near its open; targets are the opening price and the liquidity around the open, and range expectations are small. "Reversal candle, that's what today is. A large wick and a small body, you see that? A large opposing run. Price is likely to close near its open."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: On an inside-type day the only reference points are previous day high, previous day low and the EQ. "Yeah, so on a day like this, really your reference points are previous day high, previous day low, EQ."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Pick the weakest index for continuation shorts (or the middle one); never trade the lagging/strongest asset. "I never trade the very lagging asset."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: If a setup lacks the sweep it needs mechanically, SMT with the other indices lets you still treat the candle as a candle 2 / reversal candle. "But because of the SMT, you can still treat this like a candle too, as a reversal candle."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: For a late continuation after the first target, the weakest asset needs SMT: a stronger asset (YM/ES) must run its previous high first; he dislikes these because he prefers to be in before the expansion. "I'm not a personal fan of these trades because I like to be in before the expansion, not kind of a later continuation of it, but that's the only option there for me."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Short into the target, not after it is hit; once the target is hit, the move is either done (consolidation) or needs a fresh reason to continue. "I'm not a huge fan of trying to short after I hit a target, right? I want to short into the target."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: When choosing the downside target, take the consolidation low (the easy low) rather than a V-shaped protected low, which is harder to reach. "Because to me, this is more of a V shape. Like I said, it's harder to get to this low. This is the easy low to get to."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: After an expansion into a level, expect a new phase of price: consolidation or a retracement into a gap, which should hold for a continuation. "What can we look for after expansion into a level? A new phase of price. You want to see a consolidation or retracement. Where would you want to see a retracement? Into a gap."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Small wick on the reversal candle supports expansion; a large wick makes it a reversal candle and you wait for the expansion. For continuation, the candle should hold/respect the EQ, then the expansion candle must close below the level. "If it has a large wick, right, let's say it would have gone all the way up here, what does that mean? It means that it's a reversal candle, you wait for the expansion. Since it had the small wick, and this is why I wanted to show it quickly, it has a small wick, it supports expansion lower."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: The model is fractal: the same C2/EQ logic applies on the 1m as on the daily, and on any asset. "Guys, you got to think it's all fractal. If you saw this on a daily chart, you'd say, oh, this should respect the EQ and go lower."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: If you keep getting stopped out before the move, move up one timeframe for entries (5m to 15m); if you have an invalidation to place a stop on, take the trade. "Move up one time frame. If you're on the five-minute, you're always getting stopped out. Just go to the 15-minute for entries."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: For overnight (London) setups use the 15m for entries because lower timeframes are sloppy; enter on the 15m closure through, stop on the protected swing, target the range EQ or range high. "I'm just a big fan of if I'm going to be trading overnight session. I just use the 15-minute because it's kind of sloppy."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Timeframe pairings: Daily-1H fractal if you work a 9-5, 4H-15m when free; with 4H-15m you only miss moves if you don't trade C2 in New York. "If you have to work a 9 to 5, the daily and hourly fractal, I think that's a very solid plan. And then if you're off work, trading the 4-hour and 15, I think that's very solid as well."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: A trade needs three things aligned: daily bias, structure, and the daily profile; a swept-and-reclaimed hourly low is not enough without a bullish daily profile. "All right, I need to have daily bias that lines up. I need to have the structure that lines up and the daily profile."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: TGIF profile requirements: Monday/Tuesday high, expansion through Thursday (multiple days of expansion, not expansion-pause-expansion), hits the weekly objective; still needs aligned LTF price action, ideally a sweep of the previous day low with SMT, then trade back into the range. "Normally, I like to see a sweep of the previous day low, then trading that back in."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Pre-open trades only with bias, an aligned daily profile, and an invalidation he trusts will not be swept by 09:30 volatility. "The only way I will do a pre-open trade is if I have bias, daily profile aligns, and then I have an invalidation. I trust to not be swept out by vol at 9.30."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Do not fade strong trends/breakouts (e.g. gold); wait for a swing low and trade with the trend. "Stop trying to fade this. Just trade the trend. Wait for a swing low and trade it higher."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Beginners should use a strict take profit and stop loss with no management; management adds decisions and usually costs R. "So people early on, I usually say, just have a strict pick profit and stop loss because they mess up the management."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Learning order: swing-point numbering (candle 1-4), candle 2 closure, then wick size for reversals and OHLC. "So candle 1, candle 2, candle 3, candle 4, and then learn what candle 2 closure is. That's really all you need to start, but you're going to want to focus on learning quick size for reversals and open high, low, close."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: EQ placement depends on the candle's wick (large vs small wick). "It's depending if it has a wick, a large wick, or a small wick."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: He uses premium/discount the opposite way to ICT (in expansions he does not want price to retrace up to a discount). "I don't use discount and premium like ICT teaches it. I use it the opposite way."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Protected swings fail and get re-swept (then price continues with trend) usually after significant liquidity has been taken. "It is when we have taken out some sort of significant liquidity."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Consolidation = a high and a low that price stays within for a period of time; a range's targets are its EQ and its extremes. "it's a high and a low that price stays within for a period of time."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Tools in the model: fair value gaps, highs, lows and order blocks only (no OTE, GEX, IFVG-as-strategy, double purge, quarter SMT). "I use fair value gaps, highs, lows, and order blocks. That's it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Yellow-folder news like 09:45 PMI is ignored. "I just don't really care about yellow folder news at 945, personally."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Your HTF opinion only matters at the timeframe you hold trades: a monthly bearish view is irrelevant to a 3m trade held 30 minutes, relevant to a 4H entry. "If you're trading the four-hour as an entry, sure, then that starts to matter. It depends where your intraday timeframe is"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: His NY-open routine: get to the chart (~09:25), look at the daily and daily profile for about three minutes. "Get to chart. Look at it for maybe three minutes. That's it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: At 10:00 all timeframes print new candles; re-assess whether the move is done or whether a continuation (with a tradeable swing) exists. "So now we have what, guys? We have 10 a.m. So what does that mean? New candles, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: After a reversal you need either a sweep to go the other way or a breakout and retest, evaluated after the candle closes. "we either need a sweep to go the other way, or we need a breakout and a retest. But that's after this candle closes"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Stop studying once you know the model; most failure is oversizing/tilt, not missing information. "But guys, you don't need to learn anything else. You need to simply stop doing dumb stuff."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Mistake: Taking 1m 'inversion' longs inside a consolidation in a bearish daily profile (Instagram inversion traders); breakeven never hits and price runs the stop. Fix: Read the daily bias/profile first; a consolidation at the low in a bearish day is where continuation forms, not a long.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Mistake: Fading breakouts / shorting a strongly trending gold. Fix: Trade the trend: wait for a swing low and trade higher.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Mistake: Shorting after the target has been hit (chasing). Fix: Enter before/into the target; if missed, let it go.

text: Mistake: Trading the lagging (strongest) index short when bearish. Fix: Trade the weakest or the middle asset only.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)
text: Mistake: Picking the V-shaped low as the target. Fix: Target the consolidation low, which is easier for price to reach.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-08-21)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Q: Bias for the rest of the day? A: The whole daily range is done; nothing to do unless already short. "Bro, we just went the whole daily range. Like, unless we are like, dying, like, there's nothing really to do anymore. Unless you're short already"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: When the indices diverge, short the weakest asset and do not trade the lagging (strongest) one against your bias. "I don't trade the lagging asset. What does that mean? If I'm bearish and YM is the strongest, I'm not touching YM."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: For a high-quality expansion you ideally want the strongest asset to reverse together with the weakest. "ideally you'd want to see the strongest asset reverse within the weakest one to actually go expand."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: To avoid chasing, ask before every entry: am I entering near the higher-timeframe open? Entering at the low of an expansion candle is where most losses come from. "the easiest thing to keep you out of trades that you're chasing is ask this question, am I entering near the higher timeframe open?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Continuations are easier because a new candle opens and you enter around its opening price. "That's why a lot of times the continuation is easier where you have a new candle open and then you're entering around that opening price, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: If you are trading candle 3, it is not a reversal candle, and you are far from the opening price, usually wait for the new candle open. "you are trading candle 3, and it's not a reversal candle. You're not around the opening price. So a lot of times, that's when you like to wait for the new candle open."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: On Mondays, if he trades, he wants to enter close to the 09:30 open because that's when volatility comes in. "generally on a Monday, I like to, if I'm going to trade it, I like to be closer to the open, you know, because that's when the volatility will come in."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Stop goes exactly at the protected swing with no extra buffer; if it is taken out, the trade is invalidated. "I'm just putting my stop loss at the protected swing. I'm not giving it extra room, because if it gets taken out, that's my invalidation."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: A higher-timeframe candle with no wick is an unestablished low; treat it as liquidity, not as a low you can trust. "I mean, it's just an unestablished low."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: When there are no lows (or highs) you can trust, trade it as a range: a sweep of the range high targets the range low. "So with that, I'm trading this as a range, we sweep the range high, we go here, right, and then you expect that."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Don't short below lows (at the bottom of a move); short up high before the lows are run. "I'm not interested really almost ever trying to short below lows like this, because that's where I would take losses"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: After expansion, expansion, expansion, wait for the next higher-timeframe open or a new continuation before re-entering. "So now if you do want to look short, when does it make sense? 9.45, right? Waiting for that next higher timeframe open. Or we've had expansion, expansion, expansion. My model would say wait for a new continuation."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: A target can come from another asset: take profit on NQ when ES hits its target. "you can take profit on one asset because the other asset hits a target too, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Time-based exits: expansion candles on the 4H, 1H and 30m all end at 10:00, so 10:00 is an exit time. "What do we have on the 4-hour? Expansion candle. What do we have on the hourly? Expansion candle. What do we have on the 30? Expansion candle. You know, all of these things end at 10 a.m. So that's a time-based exit."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: The move he prefers each day is 09:30-10:00 (or 08:00-09:00 / 09:00-10:00); later moves are choppier once the day has expanded. "I prefer the 9.30 to 10 move, because go to that most days, or an 8 to 9, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Use average daily range as context for targets: with ADR ~500-600 and ~300 done after multi-day expansion and a gap, he did not expect the previous day low without more context. "What are we thinking here on an average daily range? You know, we've had some larger ranges, but 500, 600 points, let's say, right? We're at 300."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: To extend a short to the previous day low he needs the intraday low to fail and a new 4H candle that opens and makes its high first. "this low needs to not hold, and then you need to have a new 4-hour candle that open high first, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: A CISD is a closure through the series of opposite-closing candles; mechanically you wait for that closure. "Our CISD would be a closure through these candles, right? So mechanically, you have to wait for that."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: A C2 and C3 closure without a CISD is not a setup. "Candle 2 closure, there's a candle 3, right, candle 3 closure, but it never has a CISD. So there's nothing there on gold."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Intra-candle CISD entry: the HTF candle opens, makes its high first, sweeps a POI, then closes below - that swing is protected; enter there, stop on the swing, 2R or hold if the day's context supports it. "This is an intracandle change in the state of delivery. So if you're going to do that, entry would be there, my stop would be there. You can look for 2R."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Whether to hold beyond 2R depends on the day's context (here a trade down to the lows offered ~10R). "Well, what's the context of the day? The context of the day is a trade down to these lows. So if you really wanted to, there's your 10R trade, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: A protected swing is valid on the closure through the swept POI and only prints on the open of the next candle. "what's the point of interest it sweeps out it's valid on this closure through it's gonna print on the open of the next candle"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: A daily reversal candle that closes back in the bias direction sets up a next-day continuation that should respect the upper half of that day's range (for a bullish read). "It should form a continuation in respect to the upper half of today's range, and then continue higher."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: EQ measurement: on a large-bodied expansion candle measure high to low; on a candle with a large wick measure the wick. "If you have a large candle body, expansion candle, measure it from high to very low. If you have a candle with a larger wick, measure the wick."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Beginner timeframe stack: daily and H1 for bias, H4 to M15 for entry. "Most people that are just starting out, I say use the daily and H1 for bias, and then I use the H4 for M15 for entry."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: On FX (e.g. EUR) he does not go below the 15m chart; on stocks he mostly enters on the daily (daily-hourly or monthly-daily). "If I'm trading, like, anything like Euro, something like that, I'm not really going lower than a 15-minute."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: He lets Monday print and does the weekly read on Tuesday; he has no view on tomorrow until today closes. "I usually let Monday print, then I do that on Tuesday."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: He doesn't predict how far price goes; he watches the closures. "I don't try to predict how far it will go. I'm just going to watch the closures, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Avoid consolidating markets; trade something that is trending. Learning when to avoid the market helps a lot. "you guys gotta learn when to avoid the market. It's gonna help you a lot, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: If a market (e.g. gasoline at all-time highs) is consolidating, it is often better to wait for the new month and for a swing to form. "I mean, you gotta see a swing form in something. A lot of times this is better waiting for the new month, if it's gonna consolidate."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: When late in a move, the alternative is the middle asset (ES): short it before it runs its low, refined on a lower timeframe. "You'd go to the one that's in the middle."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: When a range sweeps one side and then fails to form a continuation, expect the other range extreme to be taken. "When we failed the form of continuation, what happens? We go take out this range low."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: C2/C3 closures are the easiest way to get daily bias, but not the only way he uses. "That's the easiest way for people to get daily bias, C2 and C3 closures. Is that always what I do? No, because there's more advanced ways to do things."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Limit vs market entries is a process choice; missing a limit fill is part of the game. He market-enters. "If you use limits to enter and you get missed, that's just part of the game. I personally like to market enter, so that's how I do it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Once the day has made its full daily range there is nothing left to do unless you are already in. "Bro, we just went the whole daily range. Like, unless we are like, dying, like, there's nothing really to do anymore. Unless you're short already"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Vertical lines separating the HTF candles are essential to see the individual structure inside each higher-timeframe candle; he runs 4 HTF candles. title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: He keeps the indicator bias on Neutral to see both sides; set it to one side only if you're one-directional for the day. "I like it at neutral so I can see both sides, but if you're going into a day and you're like, I'm only bearish, you can just put it on bearish, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Mistake: Entering at the low of an expansion candle, after the higher-timeframe open (chasing). Fix: Ask whether you are entering near the HTF open; wait for a new candle open / continuation and enter near its opening price.

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Mistake: Trading the lagging/strongest asset (YM) on a bearish idea. Fix: Trade the weakest asset in the direction of the move (NQ).

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-07-27)
text: Mistake: Trading consolidating, choppy markets (gold today). Fix: Trade something that is trending; learn when to avoid the market.

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: I bought the indicator; sometimes I see setups but the indicator does not print. A: It is automatic. If it does not print, the setup did not qualify as a fractal setup. His model is candle 2 / candle 3 closure (early C2 optional); a setup needs the closure and the change in state of delivery (CISD) to print. "it has to have that closure and the change in the state of delivery to print to setup"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: How is the auto bias determined? A: Auto bias aligns a higher-timeframe model with the lower one. Auto Bias 1 goes up one fractal (on 5m with an H1 fractal it aligns with the H4-15m model); Auto Bias 2 goes up two (the daily-H1 model). If the daily-H1 model is bearish, Auto Bias 2 on the 5m shows only bearish setups for the whole day, hiding bullish ones. "Auto bias means it's aligning a higher time frame with a lower time frame."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: How do you make templates and put a shortcut in TradingView? A: Set the inputs how you want (his: history 1, automatic fractal, 4 HTF candles, no offset, early CISD on, rest default), click OK, save indicator template (he names his 'all'), star it so it appears in the toolbar. Templates do not update with the script, so re-save them after an update. 'Clean' is his empty-chart template; his daily template is just daily candles with EQ. "I'm going to hit save indicator template. Then I'll hit all, right?"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: Can you set up alerts? A: Enable alerts in the inputs and choose which (e.g. SMT). Add the alert on the timeframe whose closure you want: on the hourly for daily closures, on the 15m for 4H closures. He keeps a layout called 'alerts daily hourly' and creates the alert on the whole watchlist instead of one by one. "So if I want the daily closure, I'm going to be on the hourly. If I want the four-hour closures, I'm going to be on the 15-minute."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: Can you make it fewer than four HTF candles? A: No. The model needs four candles because he trades swing points: candle 0/1, 2, 3, 4. "my model needs four candles just because you have candle zero, or one, two, three, four, right? That's how I trade swing points."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: Does it handle two-stage SMT? A: An SMT formed with the reversal is a reversal SMT; another SMT forming later in the move is a continuation SMT; both together he calls double SMT. title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: What is the difference between PSP and SMT? A: PSP: the higher-timeframe candle closes bearish on one asset and bullish on the correlated one (e.g. YM).
