title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: With 4H/15m entries focused on NY and C3 continuations, there are many no-trade days? A: Correct; not every day gives a 15m entry, maybe one trade a day; that is how a mechanical system works. "You're not going to get trades every single time. That's not how it works with a mechanical system."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: What is the green rectangle? A: The (bullish) T-spot: where he wants the day's wick low to form and be held so price can open, make a low and trade higher. "The little green box is where I'm looking. I'm looking for that to be respected to form the wick low of this day."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: If a protected swing has SMT and the swing formed without interaction, and a fair value gap is showing to the protected swing...? A: That would not be a protected swing (question garbled; answer short). "That wouldn't be a protected swing."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: How do you run two sets of higher-timeframe candles? A: Lock one copy to a fractal (e.g. 15m), copy/paste the indicator, set the other to automatic or daily with offset 17, and remove the model (C2/C3/C4) from the second copy. "You're going to copy it, paste it, and you're just going to move one to automatic, or you can have it on the daily, and then just offset it 17."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: I saw it give wrong signals. A: It does not give signals, and what it prints is mechanically valid; a printed model is not necessarily one he wants to take. "just because it prints a model doesn't mean that it's something I want to take."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: How do you trade an NQ session? A: Watch his 'Intraday Reversals' video. After an intraday reversal: trade a 4H swing on the 15m chart (London), or wait for NY and trade an hourly swing on the 5m. "Either trade a four-hour swing in here on the 15-minute chart, right there. Or we could wait for the New York session, look to trade an hourly swing somewhere in there on the 5-minute."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: How does the indicator print the T-spot? A: It is coded in; stepping the replay one minute into the candle, the T-spot prints with a fair value gap in it, then the continuation prints on its own. "it prints the T-spot, what's in the T-spot, a fair value gap"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: Would you prefer early CISD? A: No, he prefers the actual continuation; takes an early CISD only when his bias is very strong. "No, I prefer the actual continuation. I'll sometimes take an early CISD in the case that my bias is that strong."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: Does it work with the free version of TradingView? A: Yes. "Does it work with the free version of TradingView? Yes, it does."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: Is there a reason to use YM/NQ instead of NQ/ES for SMT? A: He uses all three. text: Q: Can the thickness of continuation lines be adjusted? A: Yes: Protected Swings section, Width (e.g. 2), and style solid/dashed/dotted. He prefers solid. "We'll go right here to protected swings and change the width."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: Do you use the True Day Open? A: No, the normal daily open (CME/data feed), because he trades the actual daily candle. Also uses the weekly (Sunday) open for weekly profile: if the week reverses after an expansion, the weekly profile is generally to trade back toward the weekly open. "I'm trading the actual Daily Candle, so why would I use a different timeframe for my Open, right?"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Q: Gold on Friday? A: He would not trade gold on Friday there because he does not really trade reversals; only takes reversals when the bias is very strong, and this was not. "I'll trade reversals in the case that it's very strong on my bias. This isn't super strong bias."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Default behaviour: the indicator prints nothing until the candle closure; on the closure the PSP shows and the SMT is marked when it forms. "default settings, it's gonna not print anything until the candle closure."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Protected swings (new): a protected swing forms on a closure through; it is printed on the next candle's open, drawn as a dot plus a line, and new ones keep forming as price continues (trailing stop use). "Protected swings will form on the closure through. So on this candle here, that closes through, right? Once we get a closure through that, so on this next candle open, it will print that, right? And it's labeled with a dot."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Protected swings never repaint: when one is taken out it is turned gray (kept for review) and a new line forms. "The protected swings don't repaint, right? I don't repaint things because I find it dishonest, right?"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: History setting = how many past models stay on the chart; 0 shows only the most recent. He keeps 0 when actively trading, 1 in his template; panel default shows 4. "History is just going to show you how many models show up on your chart at one time"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Fractal setting: Automatic picks the HTF from the chart timeframe (1H chart -> daily, 15m -> 4H, 5m -> 1H); a fixed pair (e.g. daily-hourly) stays the same on any chart timeframe; Custom lets you choose any pair. "So default, it's automatic. So that means if I'm right here on the hourly, it's going to use the daily, right?"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Bias filter: Neutral shows bullish and bearish models; Bullish/Bearish show only that side; Auto Bias 1 only shows setups aligned with the model one fractal up (5m/H1 aligned with H4-15m), Auto Bias 2 two fractals up (daily-H1). "If you have auto bias 1 on the 5-minute, it's only going to align when the 4-hour's in line. If you have auto bias 2, it's going to go up two timeframes instead of one."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: HTF candles: count (default 4, he uses 4 because his model needs it; minimum 4), size small/medium/large or hide; offset shifts them right so two copies can sit side by side. "Default, I use four, because that's how I use it in my model."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: To overlay two HTF sets: copy/paste the indicator, lock the copy to the daily with offset 17 and turn off its model (C2/C3/C4) so only candles show. "I can offset it. I use 17, and I can lock it to the daily."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: HTF drawing options: HTF open line, vertical lines separating HTF periods, H/L lines of previous candles (he keeps off), previous EQ shown on the previous HTF candle and/or the chart (drawings type: chart, HTF candles, both). title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: He leaves early C2 off by default because learners should not trade C2 (more complex), but he personally turns it on. "I have that off by default because people learning my model, I don't really want you trading C2. It's more complex."

text: Model style settings: bullish CISD line, bearish CISD line, candle EQ, candle 1 sweep with C1 sweep display (HTF candles only, chart, or both), TTFM label size, T-spot colours. "C1 sweep, we had a lot of people asking to see the C1 on a higher timeframe candle, but not the lower."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Protected swing settings: enable, style (solid/dashed/dotted), width, bullish/bearish colours; the same width setting controls continuation line thickness. "Now, protected swings, this is one of the new settings. This is where you can choose the width of the protected swings and what you want it to look like and the color of it"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: SMT settings: display on chart, HTF candles or both; labels and size; correlated pairs Automatic (for NQ: ES and YM, shown in the table) or Custom with an optional second pair and an Inverse flag for inversely correlated pairs (e.g. dollar vs euro); SMT line style. "SMT, I'll use ES and YM for NQ. If you don't want to use the pairs I selected, you can turn off automatic and turn it to custom."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: PSP (new): enable and choose candle 1, candle 2 or both; on the chart only 'C2+PSP' is labelled; to see which candle is the PSP look at the HTF candles. "it will only display C2 plus a PSP if you want to see what the PSP is. You have to look on the higher term from candles here"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: PSP definition: the HTF candle closes bearish on one asset and bullish on its correlated asset; SMT is a divergence between the assets. "SMT is a divergence between the assets."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Session filter: restrict printed setups to a session (e.g. New York only) so nothing prints while you are asleep. "Turn on a filter and filter it only for New York session. You won't see anything else in your chart but setups that occur in New York session."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Calculation bars sets how many bars back the script calculates; lower it if slow. He uses about 2,000. "Calculation bars is how many bars it calculates back."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: A setup prints only if it qualifies as a fractal setup: candle closure plus a change in state of delivery (CISD). "If it doesn't have both of those, it's not going to."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Continuations are printed only for a limited time after the model; a continuation that forms too late into the move, or does not meet the demands, is not marked. "this one forms too late into the move because I mark them out specifically."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Continuation labels are shown only for continuations that form in a fair value gap. "we just label the ones that are in a fair value gap, right?"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: T-spot box: the area where he wants the daily candle's wick to form (bearish gray box for a high, green box for a bullish wick low to be held) before price trades away. "when this shows up and I have this gray box, I'm looking for the wick of the daily candle to essentially try to form somewhere in this area"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: SMT naming: reversal SMT forms with the reversal (indicator shows it on the CISD); continuation SMT forms later in the move (prints live once the correlated asset takes the level); both = double SMT. "That will be a reversal SMT because it's an SMT formed with the reversal."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Standard-deviation projections: off by default (he keeps them off); can be drawn from wicks or bodies. "I prefer to just have them off on my indicator."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Alerts: enable alerts and pick types in the inputs; create the alert while on the entry timeframe of the pair (hourly chart for daily closures, 15m for 4H) and add it to the whole watchlist. "instead of doing it one by one, you can create an alert on the watch list."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: The indicator gives no signals, stops or targets and has no win rate; it marks his model mechanically, and a printed model is not automatically one to take. "There is, in fact, no win rate for the indicator."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: The indicator is kept deliberately clean: no C1-C4 labels on chart/HTF candles and no HTF FVGs. "I don't want a billion things on my charts, right?"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: C1 is not marked by the indicator; it is just the liquidity for candle 2's reversal. "it doesn't mark out C1. C1 is just the liquidity for the reversal of candle 2."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Learners should trade only C3/C4 after a valid model prints; trading C2 comes later. "Trade CD3, CD4, after valid model prints."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: He prefers the confirmed continuation over an early CISD and takes early CISD only when bias is very strong. "I'll sometimes take an early CISD in the case that my bias is that strong."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: A doji / poor daily closure gives little bias; wait for the NY session intraday profile, or wait another day. "So usually that means I don't really have much bias going into the day, because it could really do whatever it wants."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: When price sits between protected swings on both sides, let the day form (watch Asia/London) before choosing a side. "you have a protected swing on this side you have a protected swing on the side we're in the middle so this is where you just kind of need to let the day form"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: At a liquidity target / POI, judge reversal vs continuation from the reaction: running out the opposite high versus forming a continuation, retracement or consolidation. "So what's our reaction at the low? Do we go run out this high? Or do we form a continuation or a retracement or consolidation?"

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Timeframe pairings: 30s entries pair with 10m (not 3m); 15s with 5m; automatic pairs are 1H-D, 15m-4H, 5m-1H; custom pairs such as 7H-15m are possible. "I would do just 5-minute, 15-second is what I would use. So if you're doing 30-second. I would probably use 10-minute."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: Session-dependent pairing (typed on screen): before 9:30 focus on the H4/M15 model with M15 entries; after 9:30 use the H4 chart with LTF fractals H1-M5 or M30-M3. Daily/H1 for bias. "Something like that is how I would do it if you want to master a 4-hour candle."

title: TTrades Indicator Updates - Walkthrough and Q&A (2026-07-26)
text: After an intraday reversal, either trade the 4H swing on the 15m (London) or wait for NY and trade an hourly swing on the 5m. "Or we could wait for the New York session, look to trade an hourly swing somewhere in there on the 5-minute."

title: New York Open Live Q&A with NickDoesFutures (2026-06-17)
text: When price breaks back over the protected high of a bearish trend, the trend is over and the market becomes chop; stop trading the idea. "When ES broke over this high, that tells me that this bearish trend is over. And so, for me, it becomes a chop."

title: New York Open Live Q&A with NickDoesFutures (2026-06-17)
text: A protected swing is a high that hits a point of interest and closes through the series of candles into that POI (it can be a single candle), forming a continuation; the short stays valid while price respects that high. "So as long as we remain in respect to this high, it's still valid to the short."

title: New York Open Live Q&A with NickDoesFutures (2026-06-17)
text: After a move off a POI, the 0.5 of that leg should be respected; if price trades well over the 0.5, you need a new swing and a close back lower to get another continuation, otherwise it is chop. "Because ideally, when price goes up here, it's this point of interest, closes below here, what area is respected? 0.5 of this to go lower."

title: New York Open Live Q&A with NickDoesFutures (2026-06-17)
text: Once price forms a new invalidation (lower-timeframe C2 closure and continuation), move the stop to breakeven and hold for the target. "Now you can be breakeven here, looking for a continuation to previous day low."

title: New York Open Live Q&A with NickDoesFutures (2026-06-17)

title: New York Open Live Q&A with NickDoesFutures (2026-06-17)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-05-05)
text: Q: Why not trade a reversal from those highs? A: He aligns with the daily candle. A daily candle with a small wick trading higher supports expansion higher, so he will not fade it; to trade short he needs a candle that supports expansion down. Example: gold yesterday opened with a small wick and was supported lower, so shorts made sense, and a reversal higher would have been against the daily. It's all multi-timeframe analysis. "I like to align myself with the daily candle. So if this daily candle has a small wick and it's trading higher, that supports expansion higher. I don't want to try to fade that."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-05-05)
text: Q: NQ and ES give higher-timeframe bearish SMT; what does DXY say? A: He does not use DXY for correlation with indices and does not care about this SMT. Everyone does SMT first and frames around it; he always has a model first and uses SMT only to confirm it or add confluence. ES not taking a high while NQ has is not a short if the model does not support it. His model says price remains higher; an SMT at a new low after a new continuation would be in line with that. "I always have a model first. Use SMT to confirm."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-05-05)
text: Q: Can you trade the model in any session? A: Yes. The model is just aligning multiple timeframes: daily bullish, one more timeframe bullish, then a reversal and a continuation in line with both, then enter (e.g. daily, 4H, 15m entry), basically trading a higher low. He does not care about kill zones as long as the timeframes align. "So if the daily is bullish, you want to align with that. You want to have one more timeframe bullish, and then you want to find a reversal, and then a continuation in line with both of those, and then you enter. That's my model right there."

text: Q: Which session's CISD is more important, London or New York? A: There is really only one change in the state of delivery per day, and it forms the daily wick. title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-05-05)
text: Q: How long does a protected high or low stay protected? A: Each protected swing (created when a candle closes beyond it) stays protected until the high, i.e. the target or opposing extreme, is taken. After that high is taken, price often comes back to run a protected swing and then gives a continuation, often around the EQ. He calls this a framework that happens a lot. "These all are protected until when, until this high is taken out. So once that high gets taken out, you'll notice this a lot. High will taken out and then it will come and run a protected swing and then it will get a continuation."

text: Q: How do you confirm the daily profile? A: The daily profile confirms your bias rather than being confirmed itself. To confirm the high or low of day (the daily candle's wick) he uses two things. (1) A CISD on a session-dependent timeframe: Asia = H1, London = H1/M30 (rarely M15), New York = M15/M5. (2) A higher-timeframe candle 2 closure on the H4 or H1 (never lower) at a relevant POI. Example: gold made its high of day in Asia yesterday, so he would have used an hourly change in the state of delivery. New York moves faster, especially indices, so 15m/5m confirms quicker there. "This is going to change based off time frame. So if you're in Asia, that's going to be like an H1 CISD. If you're in London, that's going to be like an H1 M30. Rarely would I go to M15, but it can be also M15. New York is generally going to be M15 slash M5."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Q: I have been blowing accounts for more than four years. How do I get out of this cycle? A: Find the actual root cause, then fix that cause: tilt/overtrading means max one trade a day (breaking that is just breaking rules); lack of a system means learn a model, any model; oversizing means size correctly. You have two choices, make change or quit; repeating the cycle just wastes years you could have fixed in year one. "And what I tell my Discord a lot is you have two choices. You can either make change or you can quit because everything else is just wasting your time."

But he needs something at the relevant level to trade away from: either a sweep of it, or an SMT (a sweep on another asset). That is why he wanted YM to take its low. "I need something at this relevant level, which is either a sweep of it or an SMT, which is a sweep on another one."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Q: What do you consider a broadening formation? A: Mark a range's high and low. Price takes out the range, falls back in, then broadens again, sweeping liquidity on both sides. It generally occurs during consolidation, before expansion away. "But it generally occurs during consolidation. That's how we start to expand away from it."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Q: How long did it take you to turn profitable? A: Around two years. "For me, it was around two years."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Q: How do you trade when the market is trending upwards? A: Look for either a sweep of a low to trade away from, or a retrace into a fair value gap to trade higher. Yesterday and today he looked for the same thing: YM to sweep a low; today it didn't happen. "All you're looking for is either a sweep of a low to then trade, or for price to retrace into a fair value gap, oops, to then trade it higher."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Q: Was it easy in the beginning to skip trading days like this? A: No, because early on he didn't know exactly what he was looking for. Now his model is well defined, so skipping is easy. "Now my model is a lot more defined, and I know what I want, so it's easier to skip."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Easiest daily bias: on the daily chart, a candle 2 or candle 3 closure confirmed by an H1 CISD is your daily bias. "Is there a candle 2 or candle 3 closure with H1 CISD? If so, that's your daily bias."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: After the daily C2/C3 + H1 CISD bias, confirm it with the daily profile; a bias without a confirming daily profile is not traded. "The next thing, though, is you need to confirm that with the daily profile, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Bullish daily profile: price opens, makes a low, then trades higher. If it opens and expands straight into objectives instead, the profile leans bearish, back to the daily open. "You want to see price open, make some sort of low and then trade higher, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: The daily profile is middle-timeframe structure, the structure of the daily candle; read it on 4H, 1H or 15m (he prefers the hourly). "So daily profile is middle timeframe structure. The daily profile is the structure of the daily candle."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: When there is no established/protected low of the day and price just trades higher into NY, New York is normally bearish back toward the daily open. "we just trade higher we get some structure like this and in new york it's normally bearish back to the daily open and around that"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: A bias alone is not enough: you need lower-timeframe structure aligned with it, i.e. a low (or high) to trade away from. "That's great to have a bias, but what do I need with a bias? I need lower timeframe structure that aligns with that."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: To frame longs you need a sweep of a relevant low or an SMT at it (a sweep on another asset); without one, a bullish bias produces no long setup. "I need something at this relevant level, which is either a sweep of it or an SMT, which is a sweep on another one."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: To frame a reversal lower at the open, price should open, go higher first (into the POI), then go lower. Opening lower first and then higher invalidates it. "If I'm wanting to frame something as a downside, I want to see price open, go higher first, then go lower. I don't want to see price open, go lower, then go higher, then go lower."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Three entry timing rules: enter before targets are hit, before the daily range is created, and around the daily open. "Enter before targets hit. Enter before daily range created. Enter around the daily open."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Relative strength: if bullish, trade the strongest asset; if bearish, trade the weakest. "If you're bullish, you focus on YM. If you're bearish, you focus on NQ, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: For a short on the weakest asset to work, the strongest asset must also reverse; if the weakest hits its low and reverses, the others are unlikely to go lower. "Like, you want to see the strongest asset start to fall, so the weakest asset can fall as well."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Use SMT as confirmation, not to frame trades: price must first displace in the intended direction before the SMT is relevant. "A lot of people use SMT to just frame things. You want to use SMT as a confirmation, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: He does not trust an equal-high SMT. "I just don't really like the equal high SMT like that because it's not that bad."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Fading the daily candle (especially on day three of an expansion) is a reversal trade and needs more confirmation; he generally avoids it. "Trying to fade the daily candle on a day three, it's not as great."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: When you have no bias or don't know what is going on, don't trade, and zoom out rather than sit on lower timeframes. "And the one thing I do is when I don't know what's going on on the indices, I don't sit on the lower timeframes, guys. I zoom out because it's not going to help me."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Hold one idea per session and wait for it to occur or invalidate; once invalidated, you are done for that idea. "I have one idea and I look for that to either occur or to invalidate, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: A valid reversal displaces away in a V-shape; the longer price takes to reverse (consolidation, failure swings), the less interesting it gets. "We want to see like a displacement away, right? We want to see a V shape, right? We don't want to see this and then consolidation, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: If price is going to go, it usually goes right away; it does not sit for an hour or two after the open. "The thing is, if price is gonna go somewhere, it just usually just goes. It doesn't sit here for an hour or two."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: A good continuation reaches cleanly over the level and closes; rejecting the level and coming back inside turns it into consolidation. "You want to see a nice, clean reach over the level? Close. You don't normally want to see price reject that level, come back in and do that because then it becomes a consolidation."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Confirmation of a continuation after a weak reversal is a new lower-timeframe swing (a new LTF high for shorts), rather than gaps or displacement per se. "Gaps, displacement, for me, it's just I look for a new high, like lower, lower time from high to form."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: A lower-timeframe FVG at a low is just that low; price reacting off it without closing below means a LTF low swept to go higher. Require a close below it on your entry timeframe (3m). "This fair value gap is literally just this low. That's all it is."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: After a close below the level, the 50% of that move should hold with no consolidation; each minute without a drop builds failure swings and lowers interest. "Then you want to see 50% of that hold. So if it already hits this, you want to see that close below. You don't really want to see it consolidate."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: For a bear idea into a new 4H candle, price should respect 0.5 of the prior wick; returning above it means bearish is wrong. "And usually I'm just focused on 0.5 of that wick, 0.5 of that wick."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: If you take a reversal, price should not return to the reversal point; he would be at breakeven once it does not follow through. "So now if I was short on a reversal though, I would be breakeven, right? Because you don't want to see the reversal return back to this point."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Once in a trade with a defined invalidation, ignore lower-timeframe closures; only check the HTF candle the setup is based on (e.g. 4H C3 closure). "Really, the only thing I'd want to look for is this is based off of a four-hour swing point. This is four-hour candle 3. So I want to see how this candle closes on the four-hour."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Read CISD using both the previous candle's price action and the current candle's; don't box off the prior candle. "Well, you gotta use both."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Macros are just new higher-timeframe candle opens (10:00 4H/1H/30m); understand HTF opens and closes instead. "All it is is a new higher timeframe candles."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Ignore DXY when trading indices; the correlation is not reliable lately. "I could care less what the dollar is doing in terms of taking a trade on the indices."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: In FX, pair a bullish currency with a bearish one, not with one that is consolidating; that is where expansion occurs. "You want to pair them opposite directions because that's what expansion occurs."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: In an uptrend, enter either on a sweep of a low or on a retrace into a fair value gap. "All you're looking for is either a sweep of a low to then trade, or for price to retrace into a fair value gap, oops, to then trade it higher."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: A POI that price closes through (e.g. a 1H FVG closed below while sweeping, not aggressively bought back) is not trusted to trade away from; closely spaced lows also need a sweep first. "Let's say we are truly going to trend today. We would respect this area, right? Makes sense, right? So that means we wouldn't really go close below this gap, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Don't trust the first retracement after price expands away from the open; it can be swept. Wait for a close over and a continuation. "because when you expand away from the open, right, I don't trust this initial retracement back in, because to me, it's like I can go sweep that."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Don't chase a late continuation at the high of the day: gold's candle 6 move into the high is not worth trading even though the 4H C3 bias is intact. "This is candle 6, like I said. So yeah, not amazing on gold."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: C5 is not normally traded; it depends on whether an open objective remains. "C5 isn't normally something I trade, it just depends if you have an open objective or not."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: A small-wick daily reversal can be traded as candle 2 if you trade C2; otherwise let it close and trade candle 3. "That would be so if you're trading candle 2, yeah. If not, you let it close and you're still trading candle 3."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Inside a range, big moves usually just draw people in on both sides; don't chase them. "when we're inside a range like this and you see the market make big moves like this, it usually is just drawing people in, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Not fitting the model is reason enough to skip a breakout; you will miss moves trading mechanically, and that is expected. "It doesn't mean it can't break out. It just doesn't fit my model to trade that breakout."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: Feel the emotion, don't act on it; emotions can't be eliminated, only not acted upon. "Feel the emotion. Wow, I spelled so bad, right? Don't act on it, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: To stop blowing accounts, identify the root cause and fix it: overtrading means max one trade a day, no system means learn a model, oversizing means size correctly. "Well, if I'm tilting or over-trading, max one trade a day."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-04-01)
text: For crypto, use higher timeframes; crypto setups sweep both sides before moving and trend less cleanly than indices. "if you're going to trade it on crypto, you're better off focusing on some higher timeframes, right?"

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-25)
text: Q: If you don't do weekly bias, how do you do weekly profiles? A: A weekly profile does not need a weekly bias. It is a series of daily biases: each day's closure sets up the next day (e.g. Tuesday reversal, Wednesday continuation). Bullish after a bullish close, bearish after a bearish close; if Tuesday looks like the high of the week, expect continuation lower until an objective is hit, then a trade back up. The fractal model already does this: C2 closure trades C3, a good C3 close trades C4, and the model does not trade candle 5. "My fractal model does this already. For instance, hey, this is a Tuesday reversal, Wednesday continuation. What else is it? It's just a candle 2 closure trading candle 3. Oh, well, then this close is good. Trade candle 4. My model doesn't trade candle 5."

title: New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-25)
text: Q: Why don't you trade consolidations? A: Trading consolidations means fading the breakout of the range, trading back into the range and to the other side. He prefers continuations and expansion; an expansion leg is easier to trade than a range. "You can trade consolidations, but when you trade consolidations, you're trading, you're fading the breakout range. So you're trading this back into the range and to the other side of the range. I just prefer to trade continuations and expansion."

text: Livestream 2026-03-11 summary: CPI news-day stream that starts at 08:26 NY, four minutes before the 08:30 release. Short-term lows of the overnight/London range (horizontal line just under the current 15m lows, above PDL) - Short-term target; also where a CISD/continuation level would sit, which is why he does not use the CISD here.; YM1! 15m gap (grey box) that the V-shape reversal retraced into - Point of interest for a swing to form and price to trade lower; SMT with NQ at the same time.; YM1! 0.5 (EQ) of the large 15m wick - Cap for the retracement; if price trades much above it, it is less likely a continuation candle and becomes a reversal-candle scenario.; NQ1! 'This is kind of a live example of how I would use one asset to confirm the other.'; DXY/6B1! 6B ran into its gap and the dollar did not: 'you can consider that SMT'.; GC1!/SI1! Silver weaker than gold; gold has SMT at the high it swept, protecting that high. Context: CPI at 08:30 NY; the stream began at 08:26. Prep order: Daily chart first: read yesterday's closure on the indices (bearish candle 2 closure, 'this daily is not strong') > Relative strength across NQ/ES/YM: pick the weakest asset for shorts (YM), the strongest for longs (NQ) > Set one draw on liquidity for the chosen asset: YM previous day low; mark it ('Previous Day Low' label) > Mark SMT between NQ and YM and draw the projected path lower > Scan other markets quickly: gold/silver, dollar then the weakest FX pairs (EURUSD, USDJPY), Bitcoin, oil; drop anything in consolidation > Sit out the 08:30 CPI release and wait for the 09:30 equity open > Drop to 15m / 1m / 3m: wait for a swing point / continuation at a POI (gap, 0.5 of the wick) with the confirming asset (NQ) reversing > Manage toward PDL (trail to 1m bars near target) with 09:45 / 10:00 as time-based exits; stop caring once the target is hit Scenarios: If CPI release at 08:30 then Do not trade it; lean bearish on the initial release but wait for the release before getting biased, then look to 09:30 for the move.; If NQ (strongest) reverses off the high it is above pre-open then That should send the weakest asset (YM), which is not above its high, into its lows / previous day low.; If YM 15m retraces above 0.5 of the large wick and hangs there then It is less likely a continuation candle; it would have to close back as a reversal candle, and the expected continuation becomes a reversal-then-continuation sequence.; If Price spends more than about two candles trying to form the continuation then Treat it as consolidation; it probably runs the high again. title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: What are the steps to profitability / when did you find your edge? A: About a year to build the model and another year to refine it. "Took me like a year to make my model and then a good year to refine it down."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: Would you look at ADR here? A: More time-based for him: 10:00 is when new timeframe candles open. "But 10 AM is when we get all the new opening of the timeframes."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: Why did you pick YM for the short? A: YM is the weakest; NQ up top, ES in the middle ranging. The whole focus was YM to previous day low; can continue until 10:00. Timeframe doesn't matter: what matters is a level to trade away from (invalidation). "YM is the weakest asset and we knew that. So our whole focus for the whole time was YM to previous day low."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: Where would you enter YM? A: A few areas. On the 1m you could have been stopped and needed to re-enter; when price is messy (NQ not reversing) use a wider stop, e.g. over 50% of the 30-second CISD. "You'd want your stop over 50% of that."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: Is it wise to take a continuation trade after previous day low got taken? A: He prefers not to trade once the target is hit, especially when most of the daily range was used to reach it (500-600 points here vs a PDH taken with only ~100 points of range used). "I personally prefer not to trade once my target has been hit."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: What do you think of NQ longs now? A: If YM reacts off PDL, NQ can go higher. YM hit PDL, then around 09:50 formed a V-shape reversal; don't trade the reversal, wait for the continuation that forms a protected swing; 10:00 open pushes it. He prefers his one-and-done move. "you don't even have to trade the reversal, you wait for the continuation, which is what? That. That forms a protected swing, right?"

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: If looking for NQ longs, do you want the 5m low taken out? A: No; in expansion you want retracement/continuation/consolidation, not the low taken. "No, ideally you don't, because here's the thing, guys."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: Let me know when bias flips. A: He doesn't know what's going on now and doesn't care; trading is about knowing segments you understand. "Trading is not about understanding everything that's going on. It's about having segments that you know, you understand what is going on."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: Is 5% a month good? A: Yes: compounding 5%/month on 100K for 4 years is about $1.04M. "People just don't understand compound interest."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: Daily C2 closure, then next day a 4H swing to a 1m/15m entry: valid? A: Yes, you can do that. "Yeah, you can do that."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: Gold is very fast; how can I enter? A: Same as everything else: slow into the low, strong reaction tells you it wants higher; first target is the protected high, then look for a continuation. "It's just the reaction here is very strong, and then it tells you that it wants to go higher."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: Price has a delayed CPI move today? A: No, there just wasn't a CPI move. "No, it just didn't have a CPI move. It's not delayed."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: Are you bearish on YM? A: He was bearish to previous day low; it hit PDL and now he doesn't care. "Now it hit previous day low and I do not really care."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Q: Do you use RTY? A: Not really; not his thing. "Do I use RTY? Not really."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Do not trade the 08:30 CPI release itself; wait for the release, then look for the move at the 09:30 equity open. "Obviously I'm not going to be participating in CPI release, but I would be bearish on the initial release at least."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: On a news morning, hold off on firming the bias until the release has printed, while keeping the daily-closure lean. "I'm going to kind of see what the release does before I get too biased."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Treat the 08:30 move as manipulation and expect 09:30 to deliver the move in the bias direction. "830 is manipulation, so I'm wanting 930 to continue lower, right?"

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: A quiet release does not change the plan; there is no 'delayed CPI move', the daily bias and draw stay the same. "No, it just didn't have a CPI move. It's not delayed."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: The 09:30 volatility comes from the NYSE equity open (stocks/ETFs start trading), which is why the NY open matters for index futures and not much for currencies. "Equity's open, NYSE open, exactly. So you have NYSE open, right, at 9.30."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: For shorts trade the weakest index (here YM) and for longs the strongest; the easiest target for the weakest asset is the previous day low. "if I had to focus on one thing, I'm going to choose the weakest asset, and the easiest target is just the previous state low, right?"

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Confirm the weak asset's move with the strong asset: the YM short needs NQ to reverse off its high; if the strong asset won't reverse, you are probably wrong. "If it's not reversing here, that usually means I'm wrong, but we'll see what happens, right?"

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Skip the CISD when its level sits at the same place as your short-term target; use other evidence instead (V-shape reversal back into a gap with SMT). "my change in the state of delivery level or my continuation level is at the same level as what would be a short-term target for me. And so if I wait for this to close, I'm literally at a target."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: With a large wick, the next candle should respect 0.5 of that wick; trading much beyond it makes a continuation unlikely and turns it into a reversal-candle scenario. "this is 50% of that wick, right, this is kind of where it caps it, right? We don't want to see a trade higher than that if this is going to be a continuation of this move."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: EQ / 0.5 of the wick tells you whether the wick is small enough for the candle to still expand mechanically. "That tells you when the wick is small enough to still expand mechanically."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Continuations should be quick; if price spends more than about two candles trying to form one, treat it as consolidation that likely runs the high again. "we want continuations to be quick. You don't want to see it hang around, then close, right?"

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Do not take blind retest entries into a POI; wait for price to form a swing point (or a strong candle 2 close with a small opposing wick) there first. "I don't want to just, I don't personally want to just retest entries"

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Do not flip the daily bias on one lower-timeframe candle; only a relevant level being hit (e.g. PDL) or the strong asset turning weak would change it. "Like, I don't switch my bias because of one 15-minute candle."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Anticipate one leg of price at a time (one draw), then react; don't predict several legs ahead. "You are just predicting one leg in price. Then you see what happens. Then you predict, right?"

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: One shot, one idea: once the target is hit he stops; continuations after the target are less attractive, especially when most of the daily range was used to reach it. "But we've used a lot of the daily range just to reach this level, right? So it makes me less interested in continuations below that level, right?"

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: As price approaches the target, trail the stop tightly to the 1-minute bar instead of giving back the move. "So a lot of times I'll just trail my stop tightly to the 1-minute bar."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Time-based exit: expansion candles (30m/15m) close into their lows/highs, so you can hold to the end of the period (09:45 or 10:00). "So if you have an expansion candle, generally you can hold till the end of the period and you're gonna be near that low, right?"

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: 10:00 NY opens new higher-timeframe candles; any new idea forms there. "So, 10 a.m. is kind of where, if you want to... Get any sort of new idea, it comes at 10 a.m."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Confirm bias by waiting for the HTF candle to form its wick, then trade away from it with a swing point or fractal model, aligning timeframes and finding a protected swing. "So all it's really about is you're aligning multiple timeframes in one direction and then finding a protected swing."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: A+ setup: candle 3 on every timeframe, an open, a reach into a POI (usually an FVG), closure through, enter with the stop at the swing. "Candle 3 on the daily, candle 3, it's just candle 3 on every time frame."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Asia is traded only on a daily candle 2 closure with a protected swing formed inside C2 before the next candle opens; enter positionally with the stop at that swing. "The only time I trade during Asia session is when I have a candle 2 closure on the daily."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Timeframe floor by session: 15m minimum for London; go lower only in New York when volatility allows; a 4H swing is entered on the 15m. "15-minute minimum for, like, London, if I ever watch that. The only time I really go lower is into the New York session when the volatility allows that."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: For a candle-2 day the London reversal should form a shallow wick (high of day); if NY runs the London high, the day is consolidation and he is not interested. "if I'm trading a candle 2, the whole idea is that we form a wick, a shallow wick, and then trade lower. I'm not really interested if price runs out this London."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: A reversal expectation is basic: from a high, wait for a lower high to trade. "Here's a high, I want to wait for a lower high to trade. That's it."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: The level to trade away from (invalidation) matters, not the timeframe; the 3m is often cleaner than the 1m. "But the whole thing, guys, about trading is you want to level the trade away from. You want some sort of invalidation."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: When price is messy and the confirming asset isn't cooperating, use a wider stop, e.g. beyond 50% of the 30-second CISD. "that's when you may have to use a little bit of a wider stop."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: After the weak asset reacts at its target, the strong asset can be traded the other way, but take the continuation that forms a protected swing rather than the reversal itself. "you don't even have to trade the reversal, you wait for the continuation, which is what? That. That forms a protected swing, right?"

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: For FX, do the analysis on the dollar and pair it with the weakest (or strongest) currency; use only the dollar as the SMT reference for USD pairs. "If dollar is bullish, you want to pair it with the weakest currency."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Skip markets in consolidation (gold, oil, crypto here); after large ranges expect small ranges; he trades expansion. "It's not really, like, guys, I try to trade expansion, right?"

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Enter turtle-soup style only with all timeframes aligned, at the sweep, with the stop right there. "You really have to enter with your stop that."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Move to breakeven only after a new protected swing forms and price trades away; too early gets retested out. "So you don't want to do it too early."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Get entries early in the candle rather than near its close. "Well you ideally get entries earlier into the candle."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: At 2R, a win rate above 50% is good; aim for few trades (one or two a week). "I just know that at 2R, if I have over a 50% win rate, I'm doing good."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Keep the chart clean: highs/lows, FVGs, opposing candles (his OB) or CISD, protected swings, SMT, HTF opens; no BOS/CHoCH. "I'll use highs and lows, fair value gap, and then opposing handles."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Psychology fix: stop doing dumb stuff; don't compare yourself with others or with cherry-picked 10R posts. "Stop comparing yourself to random people on the internet."

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Mistake: Waiting for a CISD close when the CISD level is at your short-term target, so you enter at the target. Fix: Use the V-shape reversal into a gap plus SMT as the trigger instead.

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Mistake: Copying social-media turtle-soup entries that look tight because the stop was moved after the fact. Fix: Enter at the sweep with the stop actually there, only with all timeframes aligned; most people should avoid it.

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Mistake: Moving the stop to breakeven too early, getting retested out before the move. Fix: Wait for a new protected swing and for price to trade away, then move the stop.

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Mistake: Predicting multiple legs/days ahead. Fix: Anticipate one leg, see what happens, then predict the next.

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Mistake: Taking blind retest entries into a POI. Fix: Wait for a swing point / candle 2 close in the POI showing it wants to go lower.

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Mistake: Switching bias on one 15m candle. Fix: Only switch when a relevant level is hit or relative strength changes.

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Mistake: Believing 90-100% win rate claims or expecting a mechanical model to catch every move. Fix: Accept missed moves; nobody has 100% win rate.

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Mistake: Comparing yourself to others' 10R posts. Fix: Ask where the other trades are; high-R chasers usually have low win rates.

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Mistake: Repeating what doesn't work (entitlement to the market's money). Fix: Learn from it and stop doing it.

title: (CPI) New York Open Live Q&A (2026-03-11)
text: Mistake: Holding for an extra few points near the target and giving back much of the move. Fix: Trail to the 1m bar as price approaches the target.

text: Q: Can you explain the change in state of delivery? A: [guest] On his NQ 1H week of 17 Jul: a midweek reversal, Wednesday sweeps the previous day high. In bullish order flow at the PD array, the bearish CISD is a close below the last up-close candle(s) that engaged the PD array - here the Wednesday 12:00 1H candle. Before, price respected down-close candles moving up; after, it retests up-close candles moving down. Alternatively use a breaker on the 30m: price closes below the breaker, then retests it. From there, look for sells Thursday and Friday. "So on this candle right here on Wednesday at 12, price changed state of delivery"

title: Live Q&A with AM Trades - Weekly Profile (2023-07-30)
text: [guest] Before the first high-impact news of the week expect accumulation; expect manipulation just before that news, then expansion after the manipulation. "And then always following manipulation, we look for expansion."

title: Live Q&A with AM Trades - Weekly Profile (2023-07-30)
text: [guest] Focus on 8:30 news events; FOMC at 2:30 is the exception and the only time he favours the PM session. "But you're kind of going to want to focus on the 8.30 news events. And then the odd one out is like FOMC at 2.30."

title: Live Q&A with AM Trades - Weekly Profile (2023-07-30)
text: [guest] Trade futures, not stocks/ETFs: stock daily charts gap because they don't trade Asia/London, while futures daily candles open where the previous closed. "We trade the futures chart because it's very fluid, and the daily candles start. They open where the previous day closed."

title: Live Q&A with AM Trades - Weekly Profile (2023-07-30)
text: [guest] A weekly reversal needs three things: price engaging a higher-timeframe PD array, on the right day of the week (time and price), then a 1H change in state of delivery. title: Live Q&A with AM Trades - Weekly Profile (2023-07-30)
text: [guest] Bearish CISD: after bullish order flow reaches the HTF PD array, price closes below the last up-close candle(s) that engaged it; afterwards up-close candles are retested instead of down-close candles being respected. title: Live Q&A with AM Trades - Weekly Profile (2023-07-30)
text: [guest] A breaker works as an alternative CISD: on the 30m, price closes below the breaker (down-close candles before the PD-array high), then retests it. "So that same idea, price closes below that breaker. And now we have a change in state of delivery and we can even extend that out."

text: Seek-and-destroy behaviour: price fails to displace over buy side, falls back into the range, fails to displace lower, and stays stuck in the middle of the range. "is when you just fail to displace over buy side and sell side."

title: Live Q&A with AM Trades - Weekly Profile (2023-07-30)

text: Q: How do the projections work? A: [guest] AM: projections are just a fib tool (settings in his pinned post). text: Q: Explain the low-risk sell. title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Trades aren't losers, which is what win rate is, that doesn't mean I'm hitting my take profit 60% of the time. And then the last couple of questions before we let Ben go is what entry patterns do you always look for or what is your single favorite one? And then what's your favorite timeframe for breakers? I like high timeframe breakers that price submits to over a consolidation period. I like that because a consolidation on a breaker allows an internal liquidity run to be had, so you can zoom into that price like even further. PDRAs that I like a lot, I like balance price ranges, which are FEGs that have already been filled that get revisited. Something for your journal, so that would be like this. If price wants to come back down to this fair value gap that's already been filled in, this should be a sensitive area in price. If price wants to continue going higher, it could run out these stops and fill this inefficiency. A balanced price range is just like a FVG if it was a breaker. It's a breaker FVG. But I like BPRs because they tend to be more sensitive than fair value gaps, and I like breakers.

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
