title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Livestream 2022-09-11 summary: Guest stream from the 2022 ICT era: TTrades only introduces his friend Ben and relays viewer questions; almost all teaching is Ben's. Ben's lesson is 'market fractals': a higher-timeframe 'sponsorship' model (weekly/4H point of interest, market-maker sell model) is re-found on lower 'execution' timeframes (1H, 15m, 5m, 1m) to get the same target with a much smaller stop, i.e. a higher R and shorter time in the trade. He walks a hindsight S&P 500 example (August 2022 rejection of a weekly FVG near 4325, down to the 4247 sell-side pool and lower) from weekly down to 1-minute, then a NAS100 long from Friday 9 Sep 2022 (5m and 1m entries off an hourly FVG after a sell-side raid, including a 1-minute 'silver bullet' re-entry). The Q&A covers R:R and journaling, order blocks vs FVGs vs breakers, the PD array matrix, breaker vs mitigation block, kill zones, DXY as his barometer, SMT, stop runs vs real shifts, daily bias, backtesting, impulse/retracement and external-to-internal liquidity, purge-and-revert, and win rate vs strike rate. No live trades; markets reopen during the stream (~18:00 NY Sunday). Day type: Sunday evening (weekend) educational guest stream; all chart work is hindsight/bar replay; futures/FX reopen at ~18:00 NY during the stream Higher-timeframe read: SPX500USD W bearish - [guest] Hindsight example: in Aug 2022 price rallied into an unmitigated weekly FVG (partially mitigated) under the weekly swing high; this 'weekly sponsorship' frames the short idea. DOL: First weekly target: fill to 'this wick'; second: a lower weekly fair value gap (frame shows a horizontal line near ~3910 on the weekly); SPX500USD 1D bullish - [guest] Price stopped at a weekly order block ('the largest down close candle in this consolidation that created this large energetic up move'); daily now resembles the fractal model: consolidation, buy model legs, SMR, distribution, consolidation, 'now we could be using a buy model'. DOL: Fill the fair value gap above 'more or completely'; inefficiencies, a buy-side liquidity pool and another FVG inside it; DXY 1D bearish - [guest] Rate differential narrowing (Euro raised rates that week) means other currencies gain strength and the dollar should come down; DXY also 'hopped into like a daily, weekly, monthly liquidity pool and PDRA up here'. DOL: Inefficient areas below: 'this sell side pool or this FVG' (frame shows a grey box about 105.5-106.0 on DXY daily); NAS100USD 1D bullish - [guest] Asked if he is bullish on indices: 'Temporarily, yes', because he does everything off the dollar and called dollar weakness; he was 'risk on all week' and posted it the Sunday before. Key levels: SPX500USD Weekly swing high / weekly FVG area around 4310-4325 (price label 4325.2, black line ~4310 on frames) - [guest] Weekly PD array the Aug 2022 rally tagged; sponsors the short and is the swing-high stop reference; SPX500USD Sell-side liquidity pool 4247.0 (blue line, price label 4247.0) - [guest] 2R target for the 4H FVG short, 'that's 50 points'; SPX500USD Weekly order block / line near ~3905-3910 - [guest] Drawn 'for reference later'; later used as the weekly order block where price stopped (daily bias example); SPX500USD 4H target 4112.7 (position-tool target on frame) - [guest] 4-hour target lows/imbalance; 'that's five to one'; SPX500USD 1H bullish order block, '+OB(1h)' line around ~4258 - [guest] Second target in the PD array matrix ladder after the FVG fill; NAS100USD Upper line 12535.8 (labelled OB on the 5m) - [guest] Friday 9 Sep target: 'the midway point of this order block or this buy-side liquidity pool' (4-hour order block); NAS100USD Hourly FVG, grey box about 12385-12402 - [guest] 'the only thing that stood out to me ... below price, current price, was this fair value gap'; entry zone after the sell-side raid; DXY Daily FVG / sell-side area, grey box about 105.5-106.0 - [guest] Downside draw for the dollar SMT: SPX500USD/NAS100USD [guest] Trades SPY but primarily executes on NAS; uses SPY to look for SMT 'in zones'. Secondary confluence, 'not a leading indication'.; DXY/EURUSD/GBPUSD/AUDUSD [guest] 'If DXY is making higher highs and majors like AU, EU, GU are failing to make lower lows, that is something I'll be watching.' Context: [guest] Fundamental/intermarket framing: dollar strength in 2022 came from the Fed being the only central bank hiking; the Euro hiked the past week so the rate disparity is shrinking, which he reads as dollar weakness / risk-on for indices. Weekend stream; 'Okay, market's open' at ~18:01 NY. A viewer question about planning around high-impact news was asked at the end but not answered. Prep order: [guest] Start of week: weekly chart, find the weekly draw on liquidity > [guest] Find PD arrays on the opposite side of the weekly bias that can be raided first (PO3 / market maker buy model: accumulation, sell-side delivery into a PD array or liquidity pool, then buy-side delivery) > [guest] Each day: same process on the daily; PD arrays from the 4H and 1H for the daily, from the daily and 4H for the weekly > [guest] Confirm with DXY (and SMT as secondary); skip if the dollar disagrees > [guest] Zoom down from the sponsoring timeframe to 1H/15m/5m/1m and wait for liquidity taken, shift in market structure, FVG/breaker in the right half of the new dealing range Scenarios: If [guest] a candle closes above the defending side (top) of a bearish FVG then the FVG is disrespected; until then a revisit of a partly filled FVG is still valid; If [guest] a breaker does not hold then expect price to seek the next PD array right above it, e.g. an unfilled FVG left by inefficient delivery; If [guest] price breaks below a bullish order block and then the sell-side liquidity under it then the bullish PD array matrix is exhausted; look to go back up the matrix: breaker, FVG, bearish order block, buy-side pool; If [guest] an impulse swing never retraces to equilibrium before a further extension then treat the extension as a stop hunt and expect a reaction / return to internal liquidity; If [guest] the weekly objective is reached on Thursday/Friday and price purges Thursday's high then shifts then that is his purge-and-revert setup

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Should I watch ICT's monthly core content or just the 2022 mentorship? A: [guest] Be consistent and accurate with the 2022 series first; core content adds complication and delays progress; if the YouTube model works, don't change it. "I would highly recommend being consistent and accurate with the 2022 series first."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Why isn't the big wick before it used as the swing high on the 4H? A: [guest] You can use it; it is the more conservative stop and less likely to be hit, but the candle high where the shift originated is still valid; the wick is a deviation from the range grabbing liquidity. "This wick is a deviation from the range. So they're grabbing liquidity up there."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Mitigated vs unmitigated? A: [guest] Mitigation is a revisit; unmitigated means the FVG was left open. Unfilled weekly gaps are where price seeks rebalancing, so they serve as targets. "Mitigation is just like a revisit. So when I say unmitigated, that means this fair value gap was left open."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: What is sponsorship? A: [guest] Where the original idea comes from; a weekly FVG being mitigated means the weekly sponsors the move, and weekly sponsorship means weekly targets. Without it, a 4H model sponsors a 4H move. "If the weekly is sponsoring this move, weekly sponsorship means weekly target."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Is a trade invalid when price comes back to your FVG entry? What's your invalidation? A: [guest] FVGs can be revisited, especially if not fully filled; they are less sensitive than other PD arrays. Invalidation is candle closures beyond the defending side of the FVG. "So for fair value gaps, I'm looking for Candle closes to not disrespect the defending side of the extreme."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Is aiming for 1:1 reasonable for someone who struggles to hold trades? A: [guest] He would aim higher; the only real answer is your own data from 20-50 trades at 1R/1.5R/2R. He likes 3R-3.5R so he doesn't need >50% accuracy. Journal every trade with before/after screenshots. "I like 3R, 3.5R as a sweet spot, simply because the idea is I don't want to need to be accurate more than 50% of the time."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Do order blocks or FVGs hold more weight; which should we anticipate? A: [guest] Individual choice; he struggles to see order blocks and prefers breakers and FVGs. Don't marry a PD array; use what you see and study it via journaling. An order block is the last opposing candle before an explosive move that also creates an FVG. "Don't get married to a PDRA because somebody else uses it."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Difference between a breaker and a mitigation block? A: [guest] A breaker forms after a new high (not a failure swing) and is a flipped order block; a mitigation block forms without the new swing. He doesn't study mitigation blocks. "a breaker block is simply a flipped order block."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Do you only trade the kill zones or the whole session? A: [guest] Only kill zones; he prefers the PM session, where the daily draw is clearer; he often misses AM moves and that's fine. About one to two trades a week. "I only trade the kill zones"

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: How many pairs do you trade? A: [guest] SPY and NAS, plus AU, EU, GU (UCAD a little, EG as reference). Everything must be confirmed by the dollar. "If the dollar doesn't agree with my position, I am not interested in it."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Do you use breakers only on higher timeframes? A: [guest] Lower timeframes too; there is a ladder of PD arrays and if one fails there's one right above it, often an FVG from inefficient delivery. "There's like a ladder of things that are going to be respected. And if one doesn't hold, there's literally going to be one right above it."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: What is your annual rate of return? A: [guest] Won't share; points to equity curves and foresight calls on his Twitter. "I am not going to go through my Rate of return."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Do you use SMT? A: [guest] Yes, SPY vs NAS in zones and DXY vs majors, but only as secondary confluence, not leading. "So yes, I do use SMT, but it is not a leading indication for me."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Difference between a market structure shift and a stop run? A: [guest] Zoomed in without context both look like an energetic shift with displacement and FVG; you can only tell them apart with a daily bias / draw on liquidity. "But you're not going to be able to differentiate a stop run against real direction until you learn how to figure your daily bias."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Do you use intermediate/short/long-term highs and lows? A: [guest] Not labelled; reads price without it; will study it later. "I personally haven't labeled detail like I know some people do."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Which timeframes do you use (2H etc.)? A: [guest] Executes on 1m/2m/5m, references the 2H and all timeframes, wants to trade in line with daily/weekly. Weekly analysis every week, daily every day; PD arrays from 4H/1H for the daily, daily/4H for the weekly. "So if I can trade in line with the daily timeframe using a much smaller timeframe to find my entry, I'm maximizing my RR."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Best way to backtest? A: [guest] Pick an instrument and session, use a kill zone indicator, map PDH/PDL, session highs/lows, weekly highs/lows, and watch how price delivers to them across timeframes. "map out your session highs and lows, map out your weekly highs and lows. And just watch price deliver."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Advice for determining daily bias? A: [guest] Comes with time; you don't need it right every day. Read what the daily says: e.g. price stopped at a weekly order block, the daily resembles the fractal model, so look to fill the FVG above and the inefficiencies inside it. "And you don't need to have your daily bias correct every day."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Explain impulse price swings and retracement (market projection). A: [guest] Impulse is the trend swing; retracement returns into inefficiency/liquidity inside it. Key is accurate dealing ranges and premium/discount. An extension without a return to equilibrium is a stop hunt. Price always oscillates external to internal liquidity on all timeframes. "Price will always oscillate from external to internal liquidity."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Do you use ICT's 2017 liquidity purge and revert (last three days' highs/lows)? A: [guest] Not the lookback; he uses purge and revert only at the end of a daily/weekly range, e.g. weekly objective reached Thu/Fri then purge of Thursday's high and a shift. "I don't use his look back theory."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Do you use the Fib (standard deviations) for targets? A: [guest] Not always; mostly the PD array matrix and liquidity pools. Counter-trend he targets nearer PD arrays because the shift may be temporary. "I really use the PDRA matrix mostly like liquidity pools as targets depending if I'm trading with the trade or counter trend trade."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Are you bullish on the indices? A: [guest] Temporarily yes, because of expected dollar weakness from narrowing rate differentials and DXY reacting off a daily/weekly/monthly liquidity pool. "Temporarily, yes. So like I was talking to you guys earlier, I do everything based on the dollar."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Why do limit-order liquidity pools matter so much? A: [guest] The market engineers and takes liquidity on all timeframes, but the real targets come from the daily and higher because big money operates there. "It is engineering liquidity and then taking liquidity on all timeframes simultaneously."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Do you use COT data? A: [guest] No; he confirms with the dollar and waits if it disagrees. "If a dollar disagrees, I just wait."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: If price comes to the 0.5 of the Fib and leaves, is that internal range liquidity? A: [guest] Nothing is definite; if the 50% is the only unmitigated area in the dealing range, it's a strong indication price continues from there, but price may still return to fill inefficiencies first. "If that 50 has the only unmitigated area in that price swing that you've determined your dealing range, then that's a strong indication that price will continue to go higher from there."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: What is your win rate? A: [guest] Mid-60s, fluctuating; break-evens are not counted because he scales in and moves the first position to break-even/trails; win rate is not strike rate. "Don't mix up win rate with strike rate"

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: Q: Favourite entry pattern / timeframe for breakers? A: [guest] High-timeframe breakers that price submits to over a consolidation, allowing an internal liquidity run to zoom into; also balanced price ranges (filled FVGs revisited), which he finds more sensitive than plain FVGs. "I like high timeframe breakers that price submits to over a consolidation period."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] The market is fractal: the same market-maker buy/sell model (consolidation, legs, SMR, distribution) appears inside a single leg of the higher-timeframe model. "the market is fractal, so what you see on one time frame, If you drop down to a smaller time frame, you will see the same price occurrences within that model."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Separate the sponsorship timeframe (where the idea and target come from) from the execution timeframe; find a low-timeframe model inside the high-timeframe model. "So the first model is the sponsorship. The second model is your execution."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] The sponsoring timeframe sets the target: weekly sponsorship means weekly targets. "If the weekly is sponsoring this move, weekly sponsorship means weekly target."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Zooming into the HTF point of interest for a lower-timeframe entry gives the same target with a far smaller stop: higher R and less time in the market. "Being able to identify points of interest on a higher timeframe and then recreate that model as you get deeper into price will not only allow you much higher R trades"

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] An FVG is invalidated by candle closes beyond its defending side; wicks into it and revisits of a partly filled FVG are acceptable. "So I'm looking for the top of this box. I'm looking for no candle closures above that"

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Stop goes at the swing high/low where the move originated (the shift); an outlying wick high can be used as a more conservative stop. "So this is the swing high where the move is originating from."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Don't place the stop at a swing that was just raided; use the next valid swing. "Because we can't use this one because we just raided this one."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Unmitigated FVGs (open gaps) are targets because price seeks to rebalance inefficient delivery. "Fair value gaps are places where price wasn't offered efficiently. Price is going to seek rebalancing that before, you know, leaving."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Price works through the PD array matrix from one extreme to the other; take targets in order (FVG fill, order block, liquidity pool). "Price is going to work from one extreme to the other. And in the process, it's going to go through the ladder of PD arrays."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Use only the PD arrays you see clearly and have journaled data for; don't use every ICT tool. "You don't need to use everything in ICT's arsenal."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] A breaker is a flipped order block formed after a new swing high/low; a mitigation block lacks the new swing. "A breaker block creates a new high."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] A 1:1 fixed R needs >50% win rate to break even; he prefers 3R-3.5R and tests R choices on 20-50 logged trades. "So if you have a sub-50% win rate, it's mathematically impossible to be profitable with a one-to-one R2R system."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Journal every trade with before/after screenshots and the mechanics present (liquidity taken, MSS, FVG in premium/discount, OTE); it builds confidence to hold and to enter. "take before and after screenshots of all your trades, log them"

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Define the dealing range from the swing where sell side and buy side were taken; enter in the correct side of equilibrium (premium for shorts, discount for longs). "Where did we come back above equilibrium? Here. Is this tradable? Yes. Inside your FEG."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] On the execution timeframe, wait for a secondary shift in market structure after liquidity is taken, then enter at the FVG/equilibrium of the new dealing range. "we've created a secondary shift in market structure after taking sell-side liquidity. So this becomes our dealing range once we have a confirmed swing high in."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] A shift with displacement and FVG can still be a stop run; only the daily bias / draw on liquidity tells you which it is. "But you're not going to be able to differentiate a stop run against real direction until you learn how to figure your daily bias."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] DXY is the barometer: no index or major longs against a strong dollar; if the dollar disagrees, skip the trade. "so the dollar is the barometer to everything I do if the dollar disagrees I don't take it"

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] SMT (SPY vs NAS, DXY vs majors) is secondary confluence only, never leading. "Secondary confluence for me."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Start each week on the weekly chart for the weekly draw, and look for the opposite-side PD arrays that can be raided first (PO3 / market maker buy model). "Primarily, I always start my week. I always look at the weekly. Because I'm looking at my weekly draw."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Use 4H/1H PD arrays for the daily bias and daily/4H PD arrays for the weekly bias. "And I'm looking for PD arrays in the 4-hour, the 1-hour for the daily, and the daily and the 4-hour for the weekly."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] An impulse that never retraced to equilibrium before extending marks the extension as a stop hunt; price always oscillates external to internal liquidity on all timeframes. "Price for this impulse never came back to equilibrium. So for me, this is a stop hunt."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] You are trading inside every higher-timeframe candle at once; use that to pick direction in a trending market. "even if you're trading on the 5-minute, you're still trading on the 15-minute, 30-minute, 1-hour, daily, weekly, you're still trading inside that candle."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)
text: [guest] Trade only kill zones; it is fine to skip sessions and take 1-2 trades a week. "You don't need to catch every swing. You don't need to trade every session."

title: Fractalizing Entries -Q&A with Ben - ICT Concepts (2022-09-11)

And we have elections and midterms and whatnot, which normally aren't good for the markets. So my bias is going to be down, but I want to focus on reactions to last week's lows. And if we're able to kind of slice through those, I want to target down into like 3,800, 3,700. All right. Thank you guys all for showing up. It doesn't look like there's any more questions left. So if you guys want to check out his channel, and then I will post the three links to his videos that we talked about. In the description if you want to revisit that. But thanks again, Alex, for coming on. Thank you for having me. So hope you guys enjoyed it and we'll see you guys all later. See ya. Adios.

Other topics: sizing by stop distance, dynamic daily bias, big FVGs, trend changes, choosing SPX 0DTE strikes, trend days, the box setup and volume spikes. title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: Do you take the trade on the break, before the retest of the new block lower? A: [guest] On the 1m he does not look for any confirmation; he enters at the FVG. "The trade, if you're talking about the one minute, I don't look for any confirmation in the one minute."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: You marked two intermediate-term lows; why use the second and not the first? A: [guest] As intermediate-term lows step higher, he moves the reference low up to the newest one for the break. "So as the intermediate term lows just go higher, I will move my intermediate term low higher if I'm looking for that break."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: How do you define the POI that will hold? A: [guest] Uses Strat higher-timeframe context: displacement, previous yearly lows taken, new monthly continuity; won't short against a big green month or inside a monthly inside bar (consolidation). It is less about picking the POI that must hold and more about identifying a POI and using low-timeframe entries with T1 partial + breakeven so a wrong POI costs little; he says he gets POIs right 80-90% of the time. "It's more so you need to identify your POI."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: How do you look at multiple timeframes? The 15m holds but the 10m reverses and I get confused. A: TTrades: trades the 1H and the 15/5/1; the 1m gives the earliest, lowest-risk entry but is less confirmed; ideally the breaks of structure domino 1m -> 5m -> 15m. Use the 15m for the POI (liquidity, FVGs, PD arrays) and only look at lower timeframes once in the POI. "I like to focus on our 15 minute for my point of interest."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: SMT divergence (viewer SK) A: TTrades points to his short SMT video on his channel; no explanation given on stream. "And then SK, I actually have a short video on SMT divergence on my channel"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: If you had to simplify daily bias as much as possible, what would you look for? A: [guest] Mark where the relative equal highs and lows are; on news like NFP week expect both sides taken. Be patient for big shifts in structure and big FVGs. Expect a Judas swing off the open and a reversal around 10:00 (sooner or later); want an aggressive break of structure with closes above previous highs and an FVG. Lunch consolidation creates more highs/lows to watch. Simplest is The Strat (separate video). "I want to look for where the relative equal highs are and where the relative equal lows are."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: How long has Alex been trading? A: [guest] Since freshman year of high school (about five to six years), The Strat about three years, ICT just over a year; ICT gave names to what he already did and raised his R:R. "So with ICT and stuff, it's very similar to how I've already been trading. It just gives you names for everything."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: Do you live off trading or work on the side? A: [guest] Has other income; keeps trading money in separate accounts to reduce mental pressure; lived off trading full-time earlier. "In short, I can live off trading and I do sometimes use money from trading, but I try to keep it as separate as possible"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: What criteria do you use to get into a trade? A: TTrades: a higher-timeframe liquidity run (e.g. a 15m high taken) as the reason, then drop to a 1m confirmation setup so the stop sits on the nearby highs instead of far above; refers to his 'A-plus ICT entry checklist' video. "I look for a liquidity run, so some sort of higher timeframe. Reason to get short."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: Do you do this before the market opens or during? A: TTrades: before the open he marks points of interest and higher-timeframe liquidity levels; his Mon/Wed/Fri streams are around 12:00 EST. "what I do before my morning is just mark out points of interest and higher timeframe liquidity levels."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: When taking a trade, must buy-side and sell-side liquidity be taken? A: TTrades: one or the other, or at least some liquidity level. "Yeah, one or the other, or at least some sort of liquidity level."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: Displacement versus liquidity grab: how do you tell? A: TTrades: use higher-timeframe context. On the 5m/15m you are still bullish until the intermediate-term low is taken; a run of the morning stops that doesn't continue lower and then displaces over the highs is a grab. Taking a high, moving off it aggressively and failing to break above shows weakness. "So what I look for in terms of liquidity grab versus displacement is I use my higher timeframe context."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: How do you mark liquidity levels? A: TTrades: in the morning on the 15m or hourly, look at Asia, mark where 8:30 is, look left for the obvious resting liquidity, and go up to hourly/daily as needed. Promises a video on his morning process. "mark off where 830 is, right? Look to the left and where's our liquidity resting"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: Process for adding size? A: [guest] Trust in the strategy built from nailing low-of-day to high-of-day entries with tiny stops; with 1:9 targets the same risk earns far more. Prop firm cushions let you scale micros to minis faster. The limit is mental: a big loss without full confidence makes you size down and fail to recover. "Adding size, it all comes down to like very much trusting your strategy."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: Do you love the 14-minute chart? A: [guest] No, it was a mistype. "14-minute? No, I was just a mistype."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: Which fair value gaps to take, e.g. Friday's big one from about 3975? A: [guest] A big FVG is a higher-timeframe inefficiency. Either trade a breaker off a down-close candle with an FVG through it, use the 50% of the big FVG as the POI, or focus on the structure (the sensitive low); candle bodies cut the noise. Or simply don't trade inside them. In a range, wait for real displacement below the lows before shorting. TTrades adds: with large liquidity voids on the hour he watches the 5m or 1m for setups in the OTE area. "which when you have a really big one, you totally can use like the 50% mark of it."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: How do you change gears from a bullish to a bearish trend (or back)? I'm always a day or two on the wrong side. A: [guest] Don't hold bias too hard. A sweep (one candle through and back) differs from lows being run through with many closes below and no reaction; then lower highs/lower lows confirm. After that, don't expect an FVG to hold; use FVGs only as targets and target the lows of the consolidations that built the prior move (market maker buy/sell model). Even if you miss the first leg you can catch the next. "Once you start seeing that, you don't want to get stuck in the idea of, okay, well, this fair value gap right here should hold prices, right?"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: How do you choose the best option for ES? A: [guest] They trade ES futures; he calls SPX options in Discord. For 0DTE, pick a strike that will be in the money before the target. Think of price as intrinsic value (each $ in the money = $100) plus theta value. Example: 3940 calls, target 3948 = $8 intrinsic, so paying under 4.00 guarantees +100% at target; take 50% off at +100% and let the rest run. They ended about $30 in the money (4.00 -> 30.00). "The furthest you wanna go is wherever you're gonna be in the money."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: What about days that open (bullish or bearish) and just keep running? A: [guest] First identify the strong trend day (time on charts, knowing the draw). The Strat and ICT mitigation blocks help get in; 1m/15s entries can still work. If he misses the strong open, especially with options (IV jacked up), he walks away. Days he expects to go instantly come from consolidation + buy model (example June 24): consolidation, run below the lows, FVGs, retest under the lows, shift of structure, then target the highs; breakout after a big initial consolidation and a small secondary one. He rarely buys the breakout. "So what I would heavily suggest is just walking away."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: Do you watch volume? A: [guest] Only spikes: a big volume spike while price moves lower marks demand where someone is buying; works the other way at highs. Example on ARC (as heard) daily and 1m. "What I look for is spikes in volume when prices are moving lower, and that can mark out areas of demand where people are going to be trying to buy"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Q: Any ideas for the upcoming week? A: [guest] Bearish: trading under last month's low after the monthly power of three; maximum target the marked low; watch last week's low/FVG; quarterly inside-bar shooter forming; seasonality and midterms bearish; if last week's lows break, target 3800/3700. "So my bias is going to be down, but I want to focus on reactions to last week's lows."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: A higher-timeframe point of interest is required when using very low timeframe (15-second) entries, otherwise you get lost. "But it's just important you have a higher timeframe point of interest or else you'll kind of get lost."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: He trades the 1H and the 15m/5m/1m; ideally structure breaks domino from 1m to 5m to 15m. "So you wanna see the one minute break structure that leads to a five minute break of structure that leads to a 15 minute break of structure, et cetera."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Use the 15m for the point of interest (liquidity, FVGs, PD arrays) and only look at lower timeframes once price is in it. "I like to focus on our 15 minute for my point of interest."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Entry criteria: a higher-timeframe liquidity run (a high or low taken), then a 1m confirmation setup to reduce risk. "I look for a liquidity run, so some sort of higher timeframe. Reason to get short."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Some liquidity level (buy-side or sell-side) must be taken before a trade. "Yeah, one or the other, or at least some sort of liquidity level."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Before the open, mark points of interest and higher-timeframe liquidity levels: 15m/hourly, Asia, the 8:30 mark, obvious levels to the left, then hourly/daily. "what I do before my morning is just mark out points of interest and higher timeframe liquidity levels."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Separate a liquidity grab from real displacement with higher-timeframe context: the 5m/15m stays bullish until its intermediate-term low is taken. "we're still bullish unless this intermediate term low right here is taken."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: With large liquidity voids on the hourly, watch the 5m or 1m for setups in the OTE area. "It's just when I have large areas, large liquidity voids like that, I'll use lower timeframes."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Use high-timeframe POIs (hourly, daily, weekly, monthly) and drop to 1m or 15-second charts for more precise, lower-risk entries. "I got into the lower timeframes and ICT in general just as a way to figure out how to get better, more precise entries."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Premium/discount is measured at the 50% of the larger displacement leg; a weekly FVG above that 50% is a premium POI for shorts. "So we had the weekly fair value gap in premium above that 50% mark of this larger impulse down."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Reversal setup: run above previous highs, then rejection with displacement below the previous low (market structure shift), in line with the higher-timeframe bias. "it's going to be a run above the previous highs and then a rejection with displacement below that previous low to shift us back into going lower lows and lower highs"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] An intermediate-term low is a low that filled a fair value gap (or sits between two short-term lows); a structure shift needs displacement below it. "And it's intermediate because it filled that fair value gap, right?"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Enter at the midpoint (preferred) or edge of the 1m FVG left by the displacement. "You can either short the bottom of the fair value gap or the midpoint of it. Ideally, I'm trying to go for the midpoint more often than not."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] The stop goes above the high left by the displacement, which should not be retaken; that is the widest risk he takes. "that's going to be the widest risk that I would attempt to put on for my position."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] T1 is the first lower low: take about 20% off and move the stop to breakeven; runners go to the higher-timeframe target (T2). "So if this is my T1, my T1 is where I'm gonna move stops breakeven."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Size positions by stop distance (e.g. 10-point risk = 2 ES, 3.5-4 point risk = 4 ES). "You should be sizing based on your stop loss."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] With 1:10 targets a very low win rate is acceptable; one winner covers many losers. "Since your risk reward is so, so, so high, your win rate can be Extremely small"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Weekly power of three / outside bar: after taking last week's high and rejecting, target last week's low. "So with that, I want to be targeting last week's lows for the power of three."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] If price reaches into the targeted FVG with no displacement or structure break against you, the trend is strong; hold for the lower-timeframe relative equal lows and last week's lows. "we know it's a really strong trend and we know we can pretty much hold confidently looking for your relative equal lows on the lower timeframe taken out"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] The same model works on yearly/monthly candles with the daily as the entry timeframe. "That can be traded the exact same way, but instead of using a one-minute time frame, you can use like a daily or something as your one-minute or entry time frame."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Afternoon session tends to run the highs and continue in the morning's direction after a strong morning trend. "Afternoon runs highs and then continues in the direction if we have a strong morning trend"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Volume spikes on the 15-second (or when price moves lower on any timeframe) show large resting orders / demand; context, not an instant reversal signal. "volume spikes will tell you where there's big resting orders."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Strat monthly continuity: once a new month starts printing green, don't short against it for a large move; an inside bar is a consolidation. "the second this one starts coming green, I don't want to be shorting that one"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] A consolidation is a candle inside the previous timeframe candle's high and low. "And this is defined as a consolidation because it's inside of that previous time frame's highs and lows, which is the definition of a consolidation."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Previous candles' highs (lows) are pivot targets once a consolidation breaks. "With the strat, we use previous candle's highs as our pivot target"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Daily bias: mark relative equal highs and lows; on NFP-type news expect both sides taken; wait for the Judas swing off the open and an aggressive break of structure with closes and an FVG, often around 10:00. "I want to look for where the relative equal highs are and where the relative equal lows are."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] He normally does not trade afternoon reversals. "If it comes in the afternoon, normally I don't really trade it, but this one we did."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] A bullish shift needs displacement above the intermediate high, with an FVG on the leg that takes it and closes above it. "So we know that we want to see this high get displacement above it with a fair value gap on the price leg that were to take it out."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] OTE is drawn on wicks (highs and lows), not bodies; round 'bank levels' can be used. "on the OTE, I don't really use the bodies. I use the lows and the highs"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Bias should be dynamic and change during the day as price gives information; don't hold a fixed morning bias. "Your bias doesn't have to be set in stone in the morning."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Strat 15m reversal entry: buy the break of the previous candle's high, stop at its low or midpoint. "trading the break of that previous candle's high and then using either the low of it or like the midpoint of that candle and targeting the exact same area"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] For a very large FVG use its 50% as the POI, or trade the structure (breaker/FVG) inside it, or don't trade inside it at all. "which when you have a really big one, you totally can use like the 50% mark of it."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] In a range, wait for displacement through the lows (not just a liquidity run) before shorting; then the setup (breaker/FVG) defines entry. "You want to wait for that displacement and then you don't have to guess where this high ends up."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] A trend has changed when lows are run through with many closes below and no reaction (not a one-candle sweep); after that, use FVGs only as targets. "you're getting ran through and getting tons of closes below and there's no reactions, right?"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] When a market maker buy model reverses, target the lows of the consolidations that built the move (resting stops), not the inefficiencies. "We know we're actually targeting the lows and the stop losses left behind, right?"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] 0DTE options: choose a strike that is in the money before the target, pay less than half the intrinsic value at target, take 50% off at +100% and let the rest run. "The furthest you wanna go is wherever you're gonna be in the money."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] If you miss a strong trend-day open, walk away rather than chase (especially with options). "So what I would heavily suggest is just walking away."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Box setup: consolidation, run below its lows, FVGs, retest under the lows, structure shift, then target the highs. "I just look for the consolidation, run below the lows, and I want to see fair value gaps, retest under the lows, and shifts of structure to take it higher."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] A big initial consolidation, a break and close beyond it, then a small secondary consolidation tends to launch the move (breakout trade); he rarely takes it. "Breaks above and closing above those highs and really small secondary consolidation that will send it"

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: [guest] Sizing up depends on full confidence in the strategy, built from small stops and repeated precise entries. "Adding size, it all comes down to like very much trusting your strategy."

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Mistake: TTrades: trading 15-second entries without a higher-timeframe POI Fix: Always anchor lower-timeframe entries to a higher-timeframe point of interest

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Mistake: TTrades: looking at lower timeframes too much without a higher-timeframe reference Fix: Pick the POI on the 15m; only drop to lower timeframes once price is in it

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Mistake: [guest] Thinking you have to get every move right Fix: Use high R:R so a low win rate still pays; accept losses and breakeven stops

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Mistake: [guest] Fixed size regardless of stop distance Fix: Size by stop distance

title: Q&A Live with Alex's Options - ICT + Strat (2022-09-04)
text: Mistake: [guest] Holding a rigid morning bias and refusing anything else Fix: Keep bias dynamic and let price update it through the day

Prep order: higher-timeframe narrative first: which side of the curve (buy side / sell side), premium vs discount, liquidity run into an FVG > points of interest on the 15m and 1h > wait for the entry to form during a kill zone (8:30-11:00 NY) > drop to 5m / 1m / 15-second only at a point of interest for a confirmation entry (aggressive move and structure break, then a retracement) Scenarios: If [guest] ES stays below 4080 then look for bearish entries; If [guest] ES retraces back up into the edge of the balance area then look for shorts; otherwise play intraday with a slight short bias; If ES bounces Monday/Tuesday then TTrades would like that retracement up before price goes lower; If ES re-enters a balance area / range from outside then [guest] target the point of control, then the far edge of the balance area

text: Q: What is your usual risk-to-reward? A: Over 2R; moves to break-even at 2R. (Speaker not clear from the transcript.) "my usual wrist reward ratio is over 2R. That's where I try to, I go break even at 2R."

title: ICT + Orderflow - Q&A with HolyAngelBruv (2022-08-28)
text: Q: Is it useful to pair order flow with ICT? A: [guest] ICT concepts give the overarching trade idea and location; footprint and DOM narrow the entry because OTE gives a broad area and you cannot see what happens inside each candle. Near the area he looks for the tape/footprint speeding up or aggressive buyers; if price sells hard and the tape shows nothing, that deters an entry. "ICT and the concepts from ICT I would more use as the overarching concepts for Like trades that I'm looking at. But then once you start zooming in, that's where I try to narrow it down to footprint and depth of market for entries."

title: ICT + Orderflow - Q&A with HolyAngelBruv (2022-08-28)
text: Q: How do kill zones work? A: They are times of day where trades are more probable or more likely to pan out. "Kill zones are just areas where trades are more probable or they're more likely to pan out just because it's the time of day."

title: ICT + Orderflow - Q&A with HolyAngelBruv (2022-08-28)
text: Q: Question about inducement. A: It is running internal liquidity. Lows run, aggressive move up breaks structure, you look for a retracement into the discount of the range; the stops run there (longs induced / shorts run) are the inducement, price runs them into the OTE and the FVG, which is the long entry, first target the (equal) highs. The range is re-anchored to the new high once that high is made. "all it comes down to is running internal liquidity, right?"

title: 8/14/22  MMXM Live with $niper  - ICT concepts (2022-08-21)
text: Q: What does your entry checklist look like? text: Q: If a small wick breaks the low, is that a break of structure? A: Need displacement: an aggressive move breaking structure that creates a fair value gap. "If there's no fair value gap, there is no potential retracement for that entry."

TTrades reviews his own Fri 2022-08-12 NQ trades (an NQ/Dow SMT long on the 1m with OTE, and 15-second scalps), trailing stops on market structure, and spends a large share of the stream on fixed-dollar position sizing with his position-size spreadsheet ($100 per trade on an Apex 50k). The ES daily is near the ~4,300 equal highs; AM sees them as a draw, not a short signal by themselves. This is pre-TTFM material and much of it conflicts with the current model (see quality.notes). Day type: Sunday evening weekend Q&A, futures closed; no live session, only hindsight/replay examples from Thu 2022-08-11 and Fri 2022-08-12 Higher-timeframe read: ES1! 1D neutral - [guest] Asked whether daily inducement means downside next: everyone's eyes go to the 4,300 equal highs; moving over them is not technically a short signal. If they are taken, look for hourly signals hinting at downside; for now it is an area to watch. Also notes the fair value gap below. DOL: 4,300 equal highs and the imbalance above them; fair value gap below as the other side Key levels: ES1! ~4,300 daily equal highs (horizontal line drawn at the late-April/May highs) - [guest] relative equal highs = obvious buy-side liquidity draw; a sweep there is only an area to watch for hourly short signals; ES1! daily fair value gap below current price (not marked on the frame) - [guest] potential draw if price turns SMT: NQ1!/Dow Jones Industrial Average Host, reviewing Fri 2022-08-12 between about 7:00 and 10:00: NASDAQ put in higher highs/higher lows while the Dow put in lower highs; he would have gone long NQ on the 1m off that divergence. Context: Weekend stream, no session. Kill zones referenced: PM kill zone 13:30 to 16:00 equity close (AM); news on Fri 2022-08-12 morning during host's scalps (he held one contract through it). AM says Bitcoin weekend price action is uneventful; wait for futures to open for volatility. Prep order: [guest] Mark higher-timeframe points of interest (premium arrays for sell models, discount arrays for buy models) > [guest] Wait for price to hit a point of interest, then 'look left' for the model narrative > [guest] Drop to the lower timeframe and look for consolidation/accumulation, liquidity left behind (equal lows/highs), smart money reversal > [guest] Wait for the intermediate-term swing point, then enter on the silver bullet fair value gap with stop beyond the swing > [guest] Prefer entries inside the kill zone; take partials at significant lows/highs and target the opposite liquidity Scenarios: If [guest] ES trades above the ~4,300 daily equal highs then do not short just because they were taken; look for hourly signals that hint at downside

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: Is the daily on ES/NQ showing inducement, so downside should come next? A: [guest] The 4,300 equal highs draw the eye and the imbalance above is a draw; trading above them is not a short signal by itself. If they are taken, look for hourly signals that hint at downside. There is also a fair value gap below. "I don't think moving over is technically a short signal."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: Do you use the opening price every 90-minute cycle? A: [guest] No. Looks at the midnight opening price, the daily opening price or the RTH open only. "I'll look at midnight opening price, but that's in daily opening price, or like RTH"

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: How to backtest gold? A: Host does not trade gold; method is the same for any market: open a 15m chart, go back to a day, mark out what you see, watch what happens when price returns to those areas and drop to lower timeframes there. Soft4FX-type tools allow real-time-style backtesting. "The way I like to do it is just go with, like, a 15-minute chart, go back to a certain day, just mark out what you see."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: Difference between market structure shift and market structure break? A: [guest] Mostly terminology. He uses market structure break for a break of an intermediate-term swing point (more significant, higher timeframe) and market structure shift for an intraday shift such as a 30m high broken after taking a low. "Breaks are going to be something more significant, like a taking of an intermediate-term swing point."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: How do you get your daily bias? A: [guest] He does not do daily bias much. He looks at weekly bias, the days of the week that should form the high/low, follows order flow, and the market maker model gives the narrative. Host adds: if not doing that, look on the daily for relative equal highs and fair value gaps where price is likely to draw. "I don't really go about daily bias as much. Sometimes I like to look into weekly bias more"

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: In the market maker buy/sell model, do you enter on the intermediate high/low or the failed swing? A: [guest] Prefers the failed swing on the second leg: the first leg's retracement to the FVG makes the intermediate-term point; the second leg gives the failed swing that targets completion of the model (the silver bullet). "I personally will look for them on the failed swing."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: Can these concepts be used on stocks? A: Host: yes, he looks at the 5m and uses OTE from low to high, but it is less clean because stocks lack the overnight market structure. Later (TSLA 2m) he adds he does not watch stocks much because of the absence of structure; an aggressive break of structure then a single up-close candle could be a short even outside OTE. "It's less clean just because you don't have the market structure from the overnight session."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: Why not trade gold? A: Host watches only NASDAQ and ES. [guest] finds enough with indexes, Bitcoin and occasionally EUR; not watching too many things is an advantage. "I think not watching too many things is an advantage."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: How do you use the market maker buy/sell model for bias? A: [guest] Mark higher-timeframe POIs: premium arrays make sell models, discount arrays make buy models. Wait for price to hit the POI, then look left; on the lower timeframe look for consolidation/accumulation, liquidity left (equal lows), a smart money reversal, then the intermediate-term high and the silver bullet FVG entry, stop above, partials, target sell side. Walked through on an ES 3m replay of 2022-08-11. "I always say wait for the point of interest and then look left."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: I can only trade from my phone because of my 9-5; what do you recommend? A: Sit on the 15m chart; when a point of interest is reached, look at the phone and go to a lower timeframe. "When you have a point of interest, then look at your phone and look to a lower timeframe."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: Explain breakers, and how many trades do you take a week? A: [guest] A breaker forms when price makes a high, then a lower low after a run; the down-close candle before the run on buy side becomes a bearish breaker once price breaks below (opposite for bullish). He takes fewer than two trades a day, around eight a week; market maker setups are rarer but high probability. 15m is the lowest timeframe for higher-timeframe narrative; hourly to daily is the sweet spot even for day trades. "Down close candles are going to be bearish breakers and the opposite stands true for bullish breakers."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: How do you manage stops while in a trade? A: Host: take the first partial at the nearby lows and move the stop to break even, or trail market structure on a 2m/1m chart under each new higher low. [guest] Moves to break even only when the first target is hit; before that he does not touch the stop even if structure shifts; then scales and lets the rest run. Host: taking 50% off at 2R and leaving the stop still nets 1R if stopped. "If I'm not hitting my first target, I'm not touching my stop, regardless of what the market shows."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: Best way to learn how price delivers? A: [guest] Backtesting: apply what you watch to a real chart, annotate moves, write down what you see, screenshot; hindsight is where you learn. "So there's no shame in going back into your charts and back testing."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: Is the silver bullet formed after the intermediate high in the sell model (and vice versa)? A: [guest] Yes, after the intermediate-term swing point is created. Later: the ITH confirms the silver bullet; place the stop near the intermediate-term high (a defended stop) and enter on the second retracement into an FVG. "It's going to be after that intermediate term swing point is created."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: Explain algorithmic / advanced market structure. A: [guest] Structure means nothing out of context. Intermediate-term swing points form when price trades back into an FVG and moves away. When bearish, want intermediate-term lows broken (MSB) and intermediate-term highs unviolated; then a short-term high/failed swing and the sell-off. It replaces basic higher-high/lower-low reading with FVGs and short/intermediate/long-term swings. Refers to ICT 2022 mentorship episodes 12-13. "when you're bearish, you're going to want to see intermediate term lows broken and intermediate term highs staying unviolated."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: I took a long on NASDAQ Thursday the 11th; what about it? A: Host: he would not take it: the entry was at the high of the day and of the week, so risk to reward is poor; he would want a run of liquidity first, then the move higher. "you're basically entering at the high of this day, which is also the high of the week."

title: Stream Q & A with AM Trades  - ICT concepts (2022-08-14)
text: Q: If starting from scratch, what would you prioritise to become profitable? A: Host: consistent position sizing. On an Apex 50k ($2,500 trailing drawdown) he risked $100 every trade, sizing contracts to the stop (e.g. 4-point ES stop = 5 contracts, 2-point = 10). With fixed risk, a 2:1 or 3:1 R:R at 50% win rate is profitable; with inconsistent size even 75% can lose. Shows his position-size spreadsheet. "just taking consistent position size allows you to let your risk to reward and your win rate play out."

text: Without a daily bias he still trades lower-timeframe market structure; a bias held against what the chart shows is useless. "Your bias does you no good if you hold on to it and don't do what the chart tells you."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: A liquidity run or higher-timeframe reasoning behind an FVG trade raises the win rate; win rate cannot be judged without the R:R targeted. "I would say some sort of liquidity run or higher timeframe reasoning will definitely give you a higher win rate and higher success."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: A break of structure only counts with displacement; without it, treat the move as a possible liquidity grab and watch whether it wicks out. "the way I kind of think of it is like a breaker structure, you got to have some sort of displacement, right?"

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: [guest] A market structure shift needs both displacement and a candle close beyond the structure; a high taken barely and closed above without displacement is not one. "you want to see one displacement and two closing above or you know below some structure for a change in trend"

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: [guest] A fair value gap in a move is itself evidence of displacement (energetic, rapid delivery). "fair value gaps themselves inherently indicate some energetic move"

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: After a strong news-driven move up, a breakdown is more likely just a higher low; demand displacement down breaking structure before calling it a reversal. "but the thing about that is it's more than likely just going to put in a higher low, right?"

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: [guest] On trend days or heavy-news days gauge trend on the 5-minute rather than the 1-minute. "using, like, the five-minute to kind of gauge trend is a lot better than the lower timeframes."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Scalp entry: an order block with a fair value gap; enter in the FVG and expect a little trade into the order block, or wait for the reaction out and play it the other way. "Take your entry into the fair value gap, expect it to trade a little bit into the order block, or you kind of wait for the reaction out and then play it the other way."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Order block = the last down-close candle before the move up (last up-close candle before the move down); it is not the same as the fair value gap. "This is our order block, is the last down close candle here before the move, or up close candle before the move's down."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: [guest] Order blocks are only expected to hold when price is working with the higher-timeframe bias. "they're really only, I guess, valid or should expect to be valid when your higher timeframe, when price is working with your higher timeframe bias."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: [guest] OTE is a 62%-79% retracement of a swing; an FVG inside the OTE of a leg gives a premium/discount entry in the direction of the higher-timeframe bias. "Optimal trade entry, which is defined as retracement between 62% and 79% from the low to the high, or vice versa."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Do not trade the middle of a range: short in the upper (premium/OTE) part, long in the lower (discount) part. "So that's why you use your OTE and either, you know, look for trades up here in the range to go short or look for trades in this part of the range to go long, right?"

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Measure premium/discount on the higher-timeframe displacement leg (bodies or wicks) and look for longs in its OTE area, ideally at an FVG. "It's the same thing. You get a displacement leg up. Where would you want to look long? OTE area. There's a fair value gap right there."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Liquidity rests at the obvious highs and lows where traders would put their stops. "Probably on this low, right? So that's where the liquidity is resting."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: [guest] Higher-timeframe highs and lows are the more significant liquidity. "higher timeframes are usually of higher significance, higher timeframe highs and lows."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: [guest?] Price runs premium to discount and back, getting there either by going to fair value gaps or by running liquidity (speaker unclear). "And the way you do that is you either go to fair value gaps or you run liquidity."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Do not trade breakouts; when liquidity is run on one side, look for the trade the other way. "The whole point of ICT is kind of to do the opposite of a breakout."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: SMT: when correlated indices diverge at a high (one makes a higher high, the other a lower high), expect a reversal and short the weaker one. "And so I'd normally prefer to short the one that's weaker, right? So I would rather short ES here."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: After running pre-8:30 liquidity and getting a lower-timeframe setup, expect at least the nearest imbalance to be hit, or the opposite liquidity. "you expect to see at least an imbalance hit"

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Use a 15-5-1 timeframe stack, with 15- or 30-second charts for refined entries; it is fractal. "Like, I personally use the 15-5-1, and then I'll use like a 15-second, 30-second, depending on what price is doing."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Very low timeframes refine entries but can make you lose sight of higher-timeframe structure. "So I would say 15 seconds can get you really refined entries, but also if you're too narrowed down on it, you can lose sight of what's actually going on."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: For a trend change, want structure shifts to domino 1m -> 5m -> 15m; with a 15-5-1 stack, ideally see the shift on the 5m (intermediate) without waiting so long that the low-risk entry is gone. "I kind of want to see them domino."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: [guest] Use three timeframes (high, intermediate, low; e.g. 15m/5m/1m for a scalper) and require the clearest structure change, with displacement and a close, on the intermediate one. "ideally, you want to see, I guess, the most confident structure changes on your intermediate timeframe at the least."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: [guest] Build bias from the 4H (daily gives little bias), then work the 15m (maybe 1H) as the highest timeframe of the day. "something like the 4-hour kind of gives me a better idea of what I think an ideal day would look like."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Retracement vs reversal is decided by a structure shift with displacement (big energetic candles breaking structure). "And the difference between retracement and reversal comes down mostly to shifting structure with displacement, right?"

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Strat combination: a 1-2-2 reversal or a 2-2 after a liquidity run, hammers/shooters off highs and lows, always with higher-timeframe reasoning. "Yeah, I'd say 1-2-2 reversals or just 2-2 after running liquidity. Look for hammers and shooters off highs and lows."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Stop: the short-term low/high beyond the entry or the candle that created the FVG. "Or short-term high above it where I'm entering, or the candle that made the fair value gap."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: After the higher-timeframe liquidity is run and structure breaks in your direction, the swept swing should hold, so a stop beyond it is reasonable. "once we break structure and continue up, and continuing up, this low should be held. We already ran the liquidity."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: [guest] Risk about 1% per trade, max three trades a day, at 2:1 R:R so a day is capped at -3%. "Just for my account, I usually risk like 1% per trade. And try to take three trades per day."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Size positions on micros so every loss is a fixed dollar amount (his eval: 4% of drawdown, $100) whatever the stop distance. "So no matter what, if my loss is just around $100, I didn't have a loss."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Trade index options off ES/NQ futures charts because futures carry the overnight structure. "just because it gives you all the overnight structure that you don't really have with SPY and QQQ charts"

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: [guest] On sub-1-minute charts a volume spike at a stop hunt of a pivot, followed by a structure break and retrace, can mark a reversal entry; volume is not useful at 5 minutes and above. "if it takes out some swing low and then the volume comes in and then it breaks structure to the upside and retraces back down then that might be you know some sort of a long opportunity on a smaller time frame"

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Backtest/demo with no money before going live (he did about 1.5 months) and do not rush. "I would definitely say if you're just learning to not kind of rush it and just focus on actually learning."

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Mistake: Trading fair value gaps alone. Fix: Combine with a liquidity run, higher-timeframe reasoning and market structure.

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Mistake: Judging a full bearish turn from a 1-minute chart, especially on news/trend days. Fix: Use multiple timeframes; gauge trend on the 5-minute.

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Mistake: Treating a barely-taken high closed above (or a wick) as a structure shift. Fix: Require displacement and a close; otherwise expect a liquidity grab.

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Mistake: Playing breakouts. Fix: Trade the opposite side after liquidity is run; breakouts only with higher-timeframe structure agreeing.

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Mistake: Taking trades in the middle of a range. Fix: Trade the extremes using OTE/premium-discount.

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Mistake: Overthinking premium and discount. Fix: Find the current higher-timeframe range (low to high) and trade from its OTE area.

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Mistake: Getting too focused on 15-second charts. Fix: Keep the 1m/5m up to stay on the right side of higher-timeframe structure.

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Mistake: Waiting for full higher-timeframe confirmation before entering. Fix: You are late and miss the low-risk entry; aim for a middle ground (the intermediate timeframe shift).

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Mistake: [guest] Taking unlimited trades per day. Fix: Cap the number of trades so daily risk is bounded.

title: Stream Q & A with Trade For Opportunity  - ICT concepts (2022-08-10)
text: Mistake: Ex-breakout traders carrying breakout habits into ICT. Fix: Expect it to take time; you are doing the opposite of what you were trained to do.

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-08-07)
text: Q: Do you also use FVGs (in addition to order blocks)? A: There are many ways to trade ICT concepts; find one repeatable, scalable setup (e.g. displacement over highs, retrace into OB near OTE in discount, go long) and only do that. "You just need to find one thing that works for you and is repeatable and scalable."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-08-07)
text: Q: How to approach the afternoon session? A: He doesn't trade it. Mark 13:00 on the chart, look back for resting liquidity and imbalances, and look for the same setups as the morning: a run of liquidity or reach into an imbalance, then a lower-timeframe setup. "I would just do it the same as any other session. Look for liquidity imbalances."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-08-07)
text: Q: Viewer: through backtesting, displacement = price breaks completely out of the order block and creates an FVG. A: Agrees: a high-probability order block has a fair value gap above it. "Yeah, so that makes a high probability order block is when you have a fair value gap above it, right?"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-08-07)
text: Q: What is OTE? A: Optimal trade entry: where to expect the pullback in a price leg. Don't look for longs in premium; in discount look for a pullback/setup in the 0.62-0.79 retracement. "Once you get in a discount, you can be looking for longs, and then you should see some sort of pullback or setup in the 0.62 to 0.79 range."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-08-07)
text: Q: Can you be wrong half the time and be profitable? A: Yes, with 2:1 reward to risk a 50% win rate is profitable. "Yeah, if you trade with a 2 to 1 risk or reward, you can be 50% win rate and be profitable."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-08-07)

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-08-07)
text: Q: Can you explain SMT? A: Two correlated assets: one makes a higher low while the other makes a lower low (NQ accumulating while ES isn't); possibly signifies a reversal. "So all it is is NQ is accumulating longs while ES isn't, it possibly signifies a reversal."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-08-07)

When we open up and just look for liquidity, run of liquidity or higher timeframe point of interest, market structure shift on five or one minute or timeframes in between, and then a retracement into a discount or premium."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: Take two to three good trades a day, or none. "good trades, you should, like, two to three, or none."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: If you missed the move and it did not retrace, don't chase it: there is no risk-to-reward left. "So once we, once I missed this morning move and saw it didn't retrace, I knew there's no risk or reward to long it up into here."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: Prefer FVGs in areas of liquidity over order blocks; an order block usually has an FVG above it, so entering the FVG lets the order block support price anyway. "I mostly just focus on fair value gaps in, like, areas of liquidity, right?"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: On the 1-minute, a single candle inside a big impulsive move can serve as a reference point (technique credited to Turbo, a third party). "when you have a big move up and then a single candle that is in there, you can use that as a point of reference."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: Breaker: an order block that price blows through instead of respecting; then look for a return to it. "Let's say instead of price kind of mitigating this right here, it just blew right through it. Then you would look for a return to it, if that makes sense."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: Timeframe stack: daily and hourly for bias, hourly for POIs, 15-minute for POIs and liquidity, 5-minute through 1-minute for entry once price reaches the area. "So I normally go daily and hourly, kind of just give me my idea for like bias, and I'll look for hourly for points of interest, right?"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: OTE: measure the displacement range; the reversal should come in discount below 0.5, with 0.62-0.79 the optimal trade entry zone; 0.5 is used for premium/discount on everything. "I use the 0.5 for everything if you watch my video on premium discount, but OTE is just displacement range, low to high, and your reversal should occur somewhere in a discount"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: Directional bias comes from HTF market structure (1H/15m): higher highs and higher lows after a smart money reversal mean bullish until the lows break with displacement. "So until these lows give with displacement, we're still bullish. That is how I determine bias. It's pretty simple."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: Mistake: Hunting equal highs/lows and liquidity on the 1-minute chart, which gets confusing. Fix: Zoom out; mark liquidity on the 15-minute.

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: Mistake: New ICT traders get sucked into the lower timeframes and watch the 1-minute all the time. Fix: Only drop to lower timeframes once there is a higher-timeframe reason (e.g. price retracing into a 5-minute FVG); keep referencing the 5m and 15m.

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: Mistake: Shorting in a discount (e.g. after a wrong bias). Fix: Only short from premium; counter-trend targets are imbalances in discount or the expected higher low.

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: Mistake: Chasing a move that left without retracing. Fix: No retracement, no risk-to-reward: skip it.

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-31)
text: Mistake: Entering on a weak structure break without displacement leads to a quick stop-out. Fix: Prefer a break where the candle closes through with displacement.
