title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: Can you explain multi-timeframe analysis / how we'd know from this? A: He watches 15m, 5m and 1m intraday for structure. Example ES Friday 22 Jul: liquidity run on 15m, aggressive breaks of structure on 1m and 5m shift lower-timeframe structure, while on 15m it is still technically a pullback; with the HTF reason (liquidity taken, bias lower) it makes more sense for it to drop. Calls it 'telescoping'. "So I normally watch the 15-minute, the 5-minute, and the 1-minute intraday, right? And so what I watch for is just the structure on them, essentially."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: How do we know if a market structure shift will happen? A: You don't know for sure that a lower-timeframe MSS will work out on higher timeframes; what you know is that you have a higher-timeframe reason to be short, you ran liquidity and got an aggressive move. Focus on speed and distance covered. "So I would focus, if you're struggling with it, focus on the speed and distance covered, right?"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: (Joseph) Struggling with changing timeframes A: If starting out, only look at the 15-minute and follow ICT's 2022 mentorship model: at 8:30 look left for where liquidity rests; targets are equal lows, lows and FVGs. Wait for a 15m run of stops, switch to the 5m for a structure shift with an FVG, use the 1m FVG if the 5m FVG is in discount when shorting. "only look at the 15 minutes to start, right? Basically go through his mentorship model."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: Explain the importance of order blocks and why they occur A: An order block is where people load their position before the move (e.g. the up-close candle, or just its body, before a move down); if the fast move leaves orders unfilled, price comes back to fill them. He doesn't use them much — focuses on liquidity and imbalances — but uses them to narrow down inside a large imbalance on the 1m, or when there is a single order block before a large move. "To be honest, I don't really use order blocks a whole lot. I focus mostly just on liquidity and imbalances"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: If there are multiple fair value gaps, which do you choose? A: Depends on risk tolerance and R:R. You are only technically invalidated when the low (the liquidity) is taken, so entering the higher FVG means a wider stop; take a lighter position so you risk the same amount of your account. "So all it really comes down to is what drawdown you're willing to risk, right?"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: Don't you think NQ will take out all the liquidity above those highs? A: Possible, and if it does it creates an SMT divergence, but he wants some retracement before going higher, unless news rips it. "the way I see it is I want some sort of retracement before even going higher."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: How to take short 1-minute scalps with a 5-minute bias? A: In a trending market use market structure: in a downtrend any up-close candle or imbalance can be risked; enter at 50% of the displacement range; go imbalance to imbalance — scalp the imbalance, risk the low of the imbalance, target the liquidity/next imbalance. In an uptrend imbalances support price; after a structure shift up-close candles resist. He no longer does this himself. "I don't personally do this anymore because I have found that I'm better to just wait for good trades"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: How do you find your daily bias? A: Imbalances and liquidity; if nothing else, mark out liquidity. Showed an hourly Twitter markup: liquidity taken, expected a retracement, not exactly right; the same concepts apply to the daily. "Looking at imbalances, liquidity, right? So if nothing else, just mark out your liquidity."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: (Pete) SMT divergences? A: Correlated indices like ES and NQ should track each other's structure; when one breaks a short-term low and the other fails, that divergence signals a potential reversal and the one that failed is stronger. He prefers to look for them on the 15-minute. "ES and NQ should follow each other, right, or track each other because they're correlated indices"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: How do you play SMT? A: At the divergence area go to a lower timeframe (5m/1m), watch structure for a setup (higher high, higher low, displacement) and take a confirmation entry; or enter at the divergence and risk where you're invalidated, which can be a large stop (~10 ES points). Time matters: 'time and price, not price and time'. "It's time and price, not price and time."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: Which symbol to trade on a divergence (the one that held or the one that swept)? A: Two views: the one that didn't make the low is stronger, or the one that took liquidity is accumulating for a stronger move. Experiment yourself. Key is where you're invalidated: on the one that held, its low; on the one that swept, arguably when the other symbol breaks its low. "That's something I would say experiment with for yourself."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: How can you trade this model if you can't look at anything below the 15/16-minute? A: Price action is fractal: use daily/4H/1H instead of 15/5/1; setups appear on the hourly but take longer. Find POIs on higher timeframes, set alerts, look for lower-timeframe setups. Showed inducement (IDM: equal lows run) plus an FVG as a long entry. "Time's fractal, right? Or like price action is fractal."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: Confirmation for entries? A: Uses the 1m or sometimes 15s. After liquidity is run he could enter immediately, but prefers waiting for a break/shift of structure, then takes the displacement range and finds a setup in its upper half (for a short). Friday's ES short also had inducement; AMTrades took it. "Once we run liquidity here, I could just like enter right when we're up here, right? But I would rather wait for a break of structure here, right?"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Q: How do you spot lower highs and higher lows? A: Three-candle pattern: a candle with a high, a candle with a higher high, then a candle with a lower high = the swing high (and opposite for lows). Don't overthink; a line chart shows structure simply. A run of liquidity with no displacement is not a market structure shift. "You have one candle with a high right here, a higher high, and then a lower high on the next side to it."

text: Q: Breaker example? A: A breaker is an order block that price went through and then comes back to: e.g. a small down-close candle that should support price; price goes above, takes liquidity, breaks down aggressively through it, and it then acts as resistance. He doesn't use breakers much; mostly FVGs and liquidity. "All it is is an order block that kind of went through."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Intraday stack is 15m / 5m / 1m: liquidity run on the 15m, shift of structure with an FVG on the 5m, entry in an FVG (1m if needed); a lower-timeframe shift can still be a pullback on the 15m, and the higher-timeframe reason decides. "if you just sit on the 15-minute, wait for a run of liquidity, look for a five-minute shift in structure, and then look for an entry into that, that will be your easiest way to kind of trade that."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: When shorting, don't use an FVG that sits in a discount; drop to the 1m for an FVG in premium instead. "that fair value gap is in a Discount and you're looking to short, this is when I would go to the lower timeframes to look for a one-minute, right, fair value gap in there"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Judge a structure shift by speed and distance covered (displacement); a move through structure without an energetic move is not a market structure shift. "that is no way a market structure shifted to the upside because there's no displacement, right? No energetic move above the market structure."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Intraday session timing: at 8:30 look left for where liquidity rests (equal lows, lows, FVGs) to define targets. "So, 8.30, right? Look to the left of 8.30. Where is the liquidity resting?"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: If you miss the first entry, a re-break of structure with a big FVG gives a secondary entry at the 0.5 fib of that leg. "use a .5 fib of that, and there's a secondary entry."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Confirmation entry: after liquidity is run, wait for a break/shift of structure, then enter in the upper half (premium) of the displacement range for a short. "looking at the displacement range, which is from here to here, and then finding some sort of setup in the upper half there, right?"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: You are technically invalidated only when the liquidity low behind the move is taken; choose between FVGs by the drawdown you accept and size down for the wider stop so account risk stays the same. "So if you're going to enter in these positions up here, you have to take a lighter position."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Order block = last up-close candle (or its body) before a down move, where orders load; he mostly uses liquidity and imbalances and uses OBs to narrow an entry inside a larger imbalance or when a single OB precedes a large move. "I like to use them if there's a single order block and a large move up or a large move down."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Scalping in a trend: go imbalance to imbalance, enter at 50% of the displacement range, risk the low of the imbalance, target the liquidity; after structure shifts, up-close candles should resist price. "While we still are targeting that liquidity, scalp the imbalance, risk the low of the imbalance."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Daily bias comes from imbalances and liquidity; at minimum, mark out liquidity. "Looking at imbalances, liquidity, right? So if nothing else, just mark out your liquidity."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: SMT: correlated indices (ES/NQ) should make the same structure; when one breaks a short-term low and the other fails, it signals a potential reversal and the failing one is stronger. Look for it on the 15m. "But I personally like to look for them on the 15-minute timeframes. It's just the easiest to see, right?"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Time matters more than price for entries: a valid confirmation at a bad time of day is still a poor entry. "It's time and price, not price and time."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Price action is fractal: the same setup (liquidity run, displacement, FVG entry) appears on daily/4H/1H; traders who can't watch low timeframes can use those and set alerts at higher-timeframe POIs. "So like I'm using the 15-5-1. Why don't you use the day, 4-hour, an hour, right? Because setups appear on the hour, it's just they take longer to play out"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: A swing high is three candles: a high, a higher high, then a lower high (opposite for swing lows); a line chart shows structure simply. "You have one candle with a high right here, a higher high, and then a lower high on the next side to it."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Inducement (IDM): equal lows (or a trendline) run inside the move before the entry FVG adds confidence to the entry. "Or actually, that's like perfect example of inducement. So that's your IDM. And then you have your fair value gap right here."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Breaker = an order block price ran through and came back to; it then acts from the other side. He rarely uses breakers. "let's say you had an order block right here and price goes through it and then comes back. That's your breaker, right?"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: When ES and NQ both offer the setup, pick the one with the better risk-to-reward (here ES, because it retraced back up further). "ES made this retracement back up into here, so risk-to-reward-wise, it's just set up a lot better, right?"

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Be wary of early-week moves in a heavy news week (GDP, FOMC): they are probably accumulation for the news. "I know there's a bunch of news, GDP maybe, and FOMC and stuff, so be wary of that because it's probably just gonna, whatever move that is, accumulate for that."

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Mistake: Shorting from an FVG that sits in a discount of the range Fix: Drop to the 1m and find an FVG in premium

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Mistake: Calling a liquidity run with no displacement a market structure shift Fix: Require an energetic move through structure (speed and distance)

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Mistake: Getting faked out by a 1m structure shift that is only a pullback on the 15m Fix: Check the higher timeframe; balance early entries against confirmation entries

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Mistake: Entering an SMT reversal blindly at the divergence Fix: Drop to 5m/1m and wait for structure plus displacement at a good time; otherwise the stop is large (~10 ES points)

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Mistake: Beginners juggling too many timeframes Fix: Only use the 15m to start, following ICT's 2022 mentorship model

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Mistake: Over-scalping imbalances Fix: He stopped scalping because he does better waiting for good trades

title: Stream Q & A - ICT concepts (2022-07-24)
text: Mistake: Trading options Fix: He avoids them because they are bad for his emotions
